definition_en: concerned with right and wrong conduct, good in behaviour, and also the lesson drawn from a story or a set of principles
core_image: 心里那把量是非的尺子
scene: 篝火旁的寓言讲完，孩子们等着大人说出最后那句话。 The fable ends with a simple moral about patience.
sceneCN: 这里是「寓意、教训」（第 3 个义项：故事传达的道理）；句意为这则寓言以一句关于耐心的浅显道理收尾。图中可辨识物件：篝火、故事书、围坐的孩子。

derivatives.zh: 由 moral 加 -ity 构成，义为「道德；道德体系」

senses.title: Concerned with right and wrong
senses.definition: relating to principles of right and wrong behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 与行为对错的准则有关的
senses.example: Most people share a basic sense of moral duty.
senses.exampleCN: 多数人对道义责任有一种基本的感受。
senses.why: The Latin stem mor- named custom, and custom is exactly where a community's sense of right and wrong is stored.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 mor- 本指习俗，而一个群体对是非的判断正存放在习俗里。

senses.title: Good in behaviour
senses.definition: acting in a way that is considered good and honest
senses.definitionCN: 以被认为是善良诚实的方式行事
senses.example: He led a moral life and never cheated anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他过着品行端正的生活，从不欺骗任何人。
senses.why: If custom supplies the standard, a person who follows it closely can be called moral, so the adjective moves from the rule to the person.
senses.whyCN: 既然习俗提供了标准，紧守标准的人就可以被称为有道德，于是形容词从规则转到了人身上。

senses.title: The lesson of a story
senses.definition: the point or lesson that a story or event is meant to teach
senses.definitionCN: 故事或事件想要教给人的要点或教训
senses.example: The moral of the story is that patience pays.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事的寓意是耐心会有回报。
senses.why: Fables were used to teach conduct, so the adjective's subject matter became a noun for the teaching itself.
senses.whyCN: 寓言本来是用来教人行为的，于是这个形容词所谈的内容就变成名词，指那番教导本身。

senses.title: Principles held by a person or group
senses.definition: the set of principles about right and wrong that someone or a group holds
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某群体所持的一套关于是非的原则
senses.example: She questioned the morals of the people around her.
senses.exampleCN: 她质疑身边那些人的道德准则。
senses.why: Customs can be counted one by one, so the plural names the separate rules a person carries.
senses.whyCN: 习俗可以一条一条地数，于是复数就指一个人所持有的那些具体准则。

intro.en: The word travels from a Latin noun for custom through Cicero's coinage and French into an English word for conduct and for the point of a story.
intro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语表示习俗的名词出发，经西塞罗的造词与法语，进入英语，用来指品行，也指故事的要点。

items.en: Latin mos, whose stem is mor-, meant custom or habitual manner, the unwritten rules a community lived by.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mos 的词干是 mor-，意为习俗或习惯做法，即一个群体赖以生活的成文之外的规矩。

items.en: Cicero is generally credited with coining moralis to render Greek ethikos, giving Latin a word for what concerns character and conduct.
items.cn: 一般认为 moralis 是西塞罗为翻译希腊语 ethikos 而造的，给拉丁语添了一个表示品行与行为的词。

items.en: Old French moral carried the adjective into everyday use for behaviour judged good or bad.
items.cn: 古法语 moral 把这个形容词带入日常使用，用来评判行为的好坏。

items.en: Middle English moral added the noun sense of a lesson drawn from a story, especially in fables.
items.cn: 中古英语的 moral 增加了名词义，指从故事、尤其是寓言中引出的教训。

items.en: Modern English moral works as an adjective for conduct and as a noun for the point of a tale or a set of principles.
items.cn: 现代英语的 moral 既是描述行为的形容词，也是指故事要点或一套原则的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same custom stem, while the near-meaning group collects adjectives of good conduct.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「习俗」词干上的词，近义组收描述良好品行的形容词。

normal.en: Latin mos, stem mor-, meant custom, so moral first described the customs a community shared.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mos 的词干是 mor-，意为习俗，所以 moral 最初描述一个群体共享的习俗。

normal.en: Cicero coined moralis for Greek ethikos, linking the word to character rather than to law.
normal.cn: 西塞罗为希腊语 ethikos 造出 moralis，把这个词与品行而非法律联系起来。

normal.en: morality adds -ity to moral: the quality of being concerned with right and wrong.

normal.en: The plural morals names the principles a person holds.

normal.en: The prefix de- in demoralize strips away the spirit that the stem once protected.
normal.cn: demoralize 里的前缀 de- 把词干曾经守护的那股气去掉。

abstract.en: A moral is a line drawn in the sand, and the point of a story is where the line sits.
abstract.cn: 道德是一条划在沙上的线，而故事的要点就是这条线画在哪里。

abstract.en: Customs harden into morals when a community stops asking why.
abstract.cn: 当一个群体不再追问为什么，习俗就凝固成道德。

abstract.en: The same stem gives morale, which shows how a shared mood and a shared code grow from one root.
abstract.cn: 同一词干还给出 morale，说明共同的士气与共同的准则如何从一条根上长出。

examples.en: Most people share a basic sense of moral duty.
examples.cn: 多数人对道义责任有一种基本的感受。

examples.en: The moral of the story is that patience pays.
examples.cn: 这个故事的寓意是耐心会有回报。

examples.en: She questioned the morals of the people around her.
examples.cn: 她质疑身边那些人的道德准则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫乱」——莫乱来，凡事讲道德；记住 moral 是道德的。

root: 拉丁语 mos（习俗、风气，词干 mor-）派生出 moralis，意为与品行有关的，经古法语 moral 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the standard drawn from custom; the senses then divide into good conduct itself, the lesson of a tale, and the countable rules a person holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是从习俗中画出的标准；义项由此分出端正的品行本身、故事的教训，以及一个人可数的那些准则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler held up against a person's conduct, marking what is allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子举在一个人的行为前面，标出哪些是被允许的。

branches.en: a ruler laid across a decision
branches.cn: 一把尺子横在决定之上

branches.en: a person whose conduct never needs explaining
branches.cn: 一个行为从不需要解释的人

branches.en: the last line of a fable
branches.cn: 寓言结尾的那一句话

branches.en: a list of rules a family keeps
branches.cn: 一个家庭守着的一串规矩

branches.en: a tale that teaches a duty
branches.cn: 一则教人尽责的故事

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for custom, a Latin adjective built from it, and two English endings that name its quality and its defenders.
intro.cn: 这个词依托一个表示习俗的拉丁名词、由它构成的拉丁形容词，以及两个分别指「性质」与「维护者」的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun mos and its derived moralis are the direct source of this whole English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 mos 及其派生的 moralis 是这一整族英语词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 而且；此外；再者（书面正式，表递进）
definition_en: used to add a further and usually stronger point to what has already been said, chiefly in formal writing
core_image: 评审表上第一条理由后面，又添上一条分量更重的新理由
scene: 评审意见先肯定方法可靠，随后又追加一条更有分量的理由。 The method is reliable; moreover, it costs less than the old one.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（书面正式地递进补充第二点）；句意为这个方法可靠，而且比旧方法花费更少；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.phrase: moreover, it should be noted that

derivatives.zh: 本词前半，由古英语表示「更多」的比较级演变而来，义为「更多；更」
本词后半，由古英语表示「在上、越过」的词演变而来，义为「在上方；越过」
与前半同词根的最高级形式，义为「最多；最」
由该最高级词干加副词词尾构成，义为「大多；主要地」

senses.title: Adding a further point
senses.definition: introducing an additional point that follows from or strengthens the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 引出另一点，它与前面的话相接或使前面的话更强
senses.example: The plan is cheap; moreover, it can be finished within one season.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案花费低，而且能在一个季节内完工。
senses.why: More adds quantity and over adds going beyond, so the adverb literally places another point on top.
senses.whyCN: 前半表「更多」，后半表「越过」，所以这个副词字面上就是把另一点摞在上面。

senses.title: Adding a stronger reason
senses.definition: used to bring in a reason that carries more weight than the one before
senses.definitionCN: 用来引入一个比前一条更有分量的理由
senses.example: The witness was credible; moreover, her account matched the records.
senses.exampleCN: 这名证人可信，而且她的陈述与记录相符。
senses.why: The word often marks not just addition but escalation, since the second point is meant to settle the matter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常常不只表示添加，还表示加码，因为第二点意在把问题定下来。

senses.title: The second argument in a chain
senses.definition: introducing a parallel reason in a debate or a written argument
senses.definitionCN: 在论辩或书面论证中引入一条并列的理由
senses.example: The policy failed on cost; moreover, it failed on fairness.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策在成本上失败，而且在公平性上也失败。
senses.why: Written argument stacks reasons in order, and the adverb signals that the stack is still growing.
senses.whyCN: 书面论证把理由按顺序摞起来，这个副词表示这一摞还在加高。

senses.title: Supporting evidence in academic prose
senses.titleCN: 学术文本中补充同向证据
senses.definition: used in research writing to add confirming evidence in the same direction
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中补上同方向的印证材料
senses.example: The samples were pure; moreover, repeated tests gave the same result.
senses.exampleCN: 样品是纯净的，而且反复测试给出了相同结果。
senses.why: Academic prose separates claims from support, and the word introduces a second piece of support.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作把论断与支撑分开，这个词引出第二份支撑材料。

senses.title: Cumulative conditions in rules
senses.definition: used in regulations and contracts to add another condition that must also hold
senses.definitionCN: 在规章与合同里再添一项也必须满足的条件
senses.example: The applicant must hold a licence; moreover, the licence must be current.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人必须持有许可证，而且该证必须仍在有效期内。
senses.why: Legal drafting accumulates requirements, and each added clause must be met as well as the earlier ones.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草会累积要求，每添一条都与前面诸条同样必须满足。

senses.title: Sentence-initial link across sentences
senses.definition: placed at the start of a new sentence to tie it to the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 放在新句子的开头，把该句与上一句绑在一起
senses.example: Moreover, the same rule applies to part-time staff.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，同一条规则也适用于兼职人员。
senses.why: A connective at the head of a sentence tells the reader how the new sentence relates to the old one.
senses.whyCN: 置于句首的连接词告诉读者新句子与旧句子是什么关系。

senses.title: Rhetorical escalation in speeches
senses.definition: used in public speech to raise the force of an argument step by step
senses.definitionCN: 在公开演讲中一步步抬高论点的力度
senses.example: The city needs more homes; moreover, it needs them now.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市需要更多住房，而且现在就需要。
senses.why: Spoken rhetoric uses the heavy adverb to make the second clause sound like the decisive one.
senses.whyCN: 口头论辩用这个厚重的副词，让第二个分句听起来像是决定性的那一个。

senses.title: Heavier register than its synonyms
senses.titleCN: 比同义说法更书面的语体
senses.definition: used where a formal tone is wanted, in contrast with lighter everyday connectives
senses.definitionCN: 用于需要正式语体的场合，与更轻的日常连接词形成对照
senses.example: Moreover is common in reports, whereas the shorter synonyms suit speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法常见于报告，而较短的近义说法更适合口语。
senses.why: The word itself is a register signal: choosing it announces that the text is formal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身就是语体信号：选用它就宣告文本属于正式文体。

intro.en: Moreover is a native English compound of more, the comparative of much, and over, used as an intensifier. It is not a Latin borrowing, so the Latin entry list is empty.
intro.cn: 这是英语本土复合词，由表示「多」的比较级与作加强成分的「在上、越过」合成，并非拉丁语借词，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

items.en: Māra was the comparative of the word for much, and it supplies the first element.
items.cn: 古英语中表示「多」的比较级提供了第一个成分。

items.en: Ofer meant over or beyond, and in compounds it adds the sense of going further.
items.cn: 这个词意为在上、越过，在复合词中增添「更进一步」的意思。

items.en: The two words first appeared as a phrase meaning beyond that, further, before they merged.
items.cn: 两词先以短语形式出现，义为「在那之外、更进一步」，后来才合并。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the merged adverb stood at the head of a sentence to add a point; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个合并的副词已站在句首用来追加论点；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Today it belongs to formal prose and public argument and sounds heavier than its shorter rivals.
items.cn: 今天它属于正式文章与公共论辩，听起来比更短的近义说法更重。

note.en: The first group shares the compound structure or the same root; the second group lists connectives that also add a point.
note.cn: 第一组共享复合结构或同一词根；第二组是同样用于追加论点的连接词。

entries.definition: A formal connective with the same job, built from further and more.
entries.definitionCN: 一个作用相同的正式连接词，由「更远」与「更多」构成。

entries.definition: The comparative that supplies the first half of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 提供这个词前半部分的比较级形式。

entries.definition: The second half, adding the sense of beyond or on top.
entries.definitionCN: 后半部分，增添「越过、在上」的意思。

entries.definition: The superlative of the same root, meaning the greatest amount.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的最高级，义为最多。

entries.definition: An adverb from the same root, meaning for the greater part.
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的副词，义为大部分情况下。

entries.definition: A lighter connective that adds a point, often in speech and often with a hint of afterthought.
entries.definitionCN: 语气更轻的追加连接词，多用于口语，常带「顺带一提」的意味。

entries.definition: A plain phrase that adds an item without raising the tone.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的追加短语，只添一项，不抬高语气。

entries.definition: An emphatic phrase that adds a stronger consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 强调式短语，用来追加更有分量的考虑。

entries.definition: A conversational phrase for one more point stacked on the rest.
entries.definitionCN: 口语短语，表示在其余之上再加一点。

entries.definition: An adverb that pushes the argument one step farther.
entries.definitionCN: 把论证再往前推一步的副词。

normalIntro.en: More plus over: one point is placed over and beyond the first, and the compound says exactly that.
normalIntro.cn: 「更多」加「越过」：把一点摞到第一点之上并越过它，这个复合词说的正是这件事。

normal.en: Stack two bricks: the second sits higher and presses the first down.
normal.cn: 两块砖叠起来：第二块位置更高，并把第一块压住。

normal.en: It always takes a comma right after it when it opens a sentence.
normal.cn: 它放在句首时，后面总要跟一个逗号。

normal.en: In reports it replaces the spoken phrase for and also.
normal.cn: 在报告里，它替代口语中表示「而且还有」的说法。

normal.en: It never inflects; only its position in the sentence changes.
normal.cn: 它从不发生词形变化，变的只是它在句子里的位置。

normal.en: A reviewer writes it when the first reason was not quite enough.
normal.cn: 评审人写它，往往是因为第一条理由还不够。

abstract.en: A second reason is not a repetition; it is new weight on the same scale.
abstract.cn: 第二条理由不是重复，而是同一杆秤上新加的砝码。

abstract.en: Formal writing uses a signpost that admits it is adding something.
abstract.cn: 正式写作会用一块指路牌，坦白说明自己正在添加内容。

abstract.en: To say moreover is to promise that the next sentence earns its place.
abstract.cn: 说出这个词，就等于承诺下一句配得上它的位置。

examples.en: The plan is cheap; moreover, it can be finished within one season.
examples.cn: 这个方案花费低，而且能在一个季节内完工。

examples.en: Moreover, the same rule applies to part-time staff.
examples.cn: 此外，同一条规则也适用于兼职人员。

examples.en: The samples were pure; moreover, repeated tests gave the same result.
examples.cn: 样品是纯净的，而且反复测试给出了相同结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「莫罗佛」——「莫」是更多，「罗佛」是越过去，多上加多、层层加码：而且、此外

root: 英语本土复合词，由古英语表示「更多」的比较级与表示「在上、越过」的词合成，十六世纪起用作句首副词；确切书面首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a simple added point through a stronger reason, a parallel argument, academic evidence, cumulative rules, sentence linking, rhetorical escalation and the word's own formal tone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯追加一点，依次走向更强的理由、并列论据、学术证据、累积条款、跨句衔接、修辞加码，最后落到这个词本身的正式语体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a review sheet where a second, heavier reason is written under the first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张评审表，第一条理由下面又写上了分量更重的第二条。

branches.en: THE ADDED POINT: a further statement is attached, often at the head of the next sentence.
branches.cn: 追加的一点：再添一句，常置于下一句句首。

branches.en: THE STRONGER PUSH: the new point carries more weight and raises the tone.
branches.cn: 更强的一推：新论点分量更重，也抬高语气。

branches.en: THE SECOND ARGUMENT: a parallel reason stands beside the first in a debate.
branches.cn: 第二条论据：论辩中与第一条并立的理由。

branches.en: THE EXTRA EVIDENCE: academic prose adds confirming data in the same direction.
branches.cn: 额外证据：学术文字补上同方向的印证数据。

branches.en: THE CUMULATIVE RULE AND THE HEAVY TONE: conditions stack in documents, and the word itself marks formal register.
branches.cn: 累积条款与厚重语体：文书里条件层层叠加，这个词本身就标记正式语体。

intro.en: Moreover is a native compound, so its parts are ordinary English words rather than affixes. The items below show the compound and its family.
intro.cn: 这是本族复合词，组成部分是普通英语词而非词缀。下列条目展示这一复合词及其词族。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries: the word is built from Old English elements and has no Latin or Greek ancestor. The list is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词条：这个词由古英语成分构成，没有拉丁或希腊语祖先，清单按设计留空。

items.example: The compound itself adds a point.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词本身表示追加一点。

items.example: A parallel compound with the same function.
items.exampleCN: 一个功能相同的并列复合词。

items.example: It adds a point in a lighter tone.
items.exampleCN: 它以更轻的语气追加一点。

items.example: It shares the root of the first element.
The adverb ending turns the superlative into a modifier.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾把最高级变成修饰语。

items.meaning: at the head of a clause, with a comma
items.example: Position alone signals that a new point is coming.
items.exampleCN: 仅靠位置就能提示有新论点要来。

derivatives.zh: 本词前半，义为「更多」
同一词根的最高级，义为「最多」
由最高级词干加副词词尾构成，义为「大多」
本词后半，义为「在上；越过」

definition_zh: 电子的；电子设备的；电子化的；电子音乐的；电子学的
definition_en: working by controlling the flow of electrons in circuits, using computer or network technology, made with synthesizers, or relating to the science of electronics
core_image: 电路板上密布芯片与细如发丝的走线，指示灯一闪一闪
scene: 超市收银台前，顾客把手机贴在读卡器上，滴一声就完成了付款。 Most shops now accept electronic payment.
sceneCN: 这里 electronic 是「电子化的、用电子手段完成的」（第 2 个义项：借助计算机与网络技术）；句意是多数商店现在都接受电子支付。

pos.zh: 形容词：电子的；电子设备的；电子化的；电子音乐的；电子学的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ic 得到，义为「电子」
由本词加 -s 构成，义为「电子学；电子器件」
由本词加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「用电子方式地」
由本词加 -ian 构成，义为「电子工程师」

senses.title: Working through circuits
senses.titleCN: 电子的；靠电子电路工作的
senses.definition: operating by controlling the movement of electrons through circuits such as transistors and chips
senses.definitionCN: 通过控制电子在晶体管、芯片等电路中流动来工作
senses.example: The lab is testing a new electronic circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室正在测试一块新的电子电路。
senses.why: The suffix -ic turns the particle name into an adjective, so the word describes anything that works by steering electrons.
senses.whyCN: -ic 词尾把粒子名变成形容词，于是这个词形容一切靠操控电子来工作的东西。

senses.title: Done by computer or network
senses.titleCN: 电子化的；用电子手段完成的
senses.definition: carried out using computers, networks or digital systems rather than paper or face-to-face contact
senses.definitionCN: 借助计算机、网络或数字系统完成，而不是纸面或面对面
senses.example: Most shops now accept electronic payment.
senses.exampleCN: 多数商店现在都接受电子支付。
senses.why: Once a whole transaction runs through chips and networks, the device adjective spreads to the activity itself.
senses.whyCN: 当一笔交易整个跑在芯片与网络上，指设备的形容词就扩展到了活动本身。

senses.title: Made with synthesizers
senses.definition: of music produced with synthesizers, samplers and other electronic instruments
senses.definitionCN: 用合成器、采样器及其他电子乐器制作的音乐
senses.example: She writes electronic music on a laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在笔记本电脑上写电子音乐。
senses.why: The instruments are the style, so the adjective naming the technology ended up naming a whole genre.
senses.whyCN: 乐器就是风格本身，于是命名这项技术的形容词最后成了一个音乐流派的名称。

senses.title: Of the science of electronics
senses.definition: relating to electronics as a branch of engineering and physics
senses.definitionCN: 指作为工程学与物理学分支的电子学
senses.example: He teaches electronic engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 他教电子工程。
senses.why: The field that studies these circuits needed a name, and the adjective before engineering supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 研究这些电路的那门学科需要名字，而 engineering 前面的这个形容词正好提供了它。

intro.en: Electronic is electron plus -ic, coined once the particle had been found; the root itself is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electronic 是 electron 加 -ic，在粒子被发现之后才造出；而这个词根本身是希腊语里的「琥珀」。

items.en: Elektron named amber, whose rubbed surface first showed attraction.
items.cn: elektron 指琥珀，摩擦后的表面最先显现出吸引现象。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and passed the root into modern science.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 electrum 表示琥珀，并把这个词根传进近代科学。

items.en: The particle name electron gave the family a solid centre.
items.cn: 粒子名 electron 为这个词族提供了坚实的中心。

items.en: Valves and then transistors made a new adjective necessary for circuits.
items.cn: 电子管以及后来的晶体管，使指电路的形容词成为必需。

items.en: The -ic form covered devices, then transactions, then music.
items.cn: 加 -ic 的形式先指设备，再指交易，最后指音乐。

items.en: Electronic now names a whole layer of daily life built on chips.
items.cn: 如今 electronic 命名了建立在芯片之上的整整一层日常生活。

note.en: The look-alike group lines up the electric family; the near-meaning group separates electronic from electric, digital and electrical.
note.cn: 形近组排开 electric 词族；近义组区分 electronic 与 electric、digital、electrical。

entries.definition: The negative particle that these circuits control.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子」，正是这些电路所控制的粒子。

entries.definition: The science of such circuits, or the circuits as goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子学」，也指作为商品的电子器件。

entries.definition: By electronic means.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「用电子方式地」。

entries.definition: Of wiring and power systems rather than of chips.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，指布线供电系统而非芯片。

entries.definition: Driven by electricity in the plain sense, as a kettle or a motor.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「用电的」，指水壶、马达这类普通用电的东西。

entries.definition: Stored as numbers; overlaps the network sense but says nothing about circuits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「数字的」，与网络义重叠，但不涉及电路。

entries.definition: Belonging to the power system, a wider and older field.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，属于更宽、更早的电力领域。

entries.definition: Run by machines; close to the transaction sense but not tied to chips.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自动化的」，接近交易义，但不限于芯片。

normalIntro.en: These hooks walk from a single electron to a chip, then to a payment, a track and a degree.

definition_zh: 加固；加强；增援；强化；使更牢固
definition_en: to make something stronger by adding material, support, or people, or to strengthen an idea or habit by repeating it
core_image: 往旧墙里再灌一根钢筋：老墙照旧立着，只是从今往后更不容易倒
scene: 台风季来临前，工人们给阳台的护栏焊上了新的钢条。 The workers reinforced the railing with extra steel bars.
sceneCN: 这里 reinforce 是「加固」（第 1 个义项：增加材料使更牢固）；句意：工人们用额外的钢条加固了护栏。场景要点：台风前的阳台、焊枪的火花、新焊的钢条。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「加固；增援；强化（训练用语）」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「加固过的；增强的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「强化物」（行为科学用语）
同根名词，义为「力；力量；部队」（reinforce 的后半部分）

senses.title: Make a structure physically stronger
senses.definition: to add steel, timber, or other material to a building, wall, or vehicle so that it can carry more or resist damage
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑、墙体或车辆添加钢筋、木料等材料，使其承重更大或更抗损
senses.example: The workers reinforced the railing with extra steel bars.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们用额外的钢条加固了护栏。
senses.why: The word is literally 'to pour force into again': strength is treated like a substance that can be added to what already stands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的字面是「把力量再次注入」：力量被当作可以往既有之物上添加的材料。

senses.title: Send extra soldiers or equipment
senses.definition: to send additional troops, ships, or supplies to a place under attack or under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 向受攻击或承压之处增派部队、舰船或补给
senses.example: Two divisions were sent to reinforce the northern front.
senses.exampleCN: 两个师被派去增援北方战线。
senses.why: The old military sense keeps the pouring image: extra force is poured into the thinning line of defenders.
senses.whyCN: 古老的军事义保留倾注图景：把额外的力量倾注进日渐稀薄的防线。

senses.title: Make an idea, argument, or belief stronger
senses.definition: to make an argument, impression, or belief stronger by adding support, facts, or repetition
senses.definitionCN: 通过补充论据、事实或重复，使论证、印象或信念更有力
senses.example: The latest data reinforces the case for earlier screening.
senses.exampleCN: 最新数据强化了提前筛查的主张。
senses.why: Arguments are treated like walls: each new fact is another bar poured into the same structure.
senses.whyCN: 论证被当作墙来对待：每一条新事实都是灌进同一结构的又一根钢筋。

senses.title: Strengthen a habit by repeating it
senses.definition: to make a pattern of behaviour more likely to happen again, especially by rewarding it
senses.definitionCN: 通过奖励等方式，使某种行为模式更有可能再次发生
senses.example: Praising children promptly reinforces their good habits.
senses.exampleCN: 及时表扬能强化孩子的好习惯。
senses.why: Psychology borrows the builder's verb: each reward is poured into the habit's wall, so it stands a little higher.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借来建筑动词：每一次奖励都灌进习惯之墙，使它又高了一分。

senses.title: Confirm what already exists
senses.definition: to make an existing impression or attitude firmer, often without intending to, as in reinforce stereotypes
senses.definitionCN: 使已有的印象或态度更顽固，常非有意为之，如 reinforce stereotypes
senses.example: Comedies that joke the same way reinforce old stereotypes about the region.
senses.exampleCN: 以同样方式开玩笑的喜剧加深了关于该地区的旧成见。
senses.why: The wall grows even when no one means to build: repeated contact pours in another layer, and the prejudice hardens.
senses.whyCN: 即便无人有意砌墙，墙也会长高：重复的接触又灌进一层，偏见随之凝固。

intro.en: Reinforce comes from Old French renforcier 'to strengthen again', from re- 'again' + enforcier 'to strengthen', from en- 'in' + force, from Latin fortia, the neuter plural of fortis 'strong'. The earliest English uses are military: to reinforce was to pour more men into a battle.
intro.cn: reinforce 来自古法语 renforcier「再度加强」，由 re-「再」加 enforcier「加强」构成，enforcier 出自 en-「在……里」加 force，force 上溯拉丁语 fortia（fortis「强壮的」的中性复数）。最早的英语用法是军事的：reinforce 即向战场再投入兵力。

items.en: The reconstructed root *dʰerǵʰ- or *bʰerǵʰ- 'to be strong, hold high' underlies Latin fortis and its family fort, fortify, comfort, effort.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根「强壮、高举」生成了拉丁语 fortis 及其家族 fort、fortify、comfort、effort。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong, brave'; its neuter plural fortia, 'strengths', passed into Vulgar Latin as a feminine noun forza, the source of French force.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮的、勇敢的」；其中性复数 fortia（诸般力量）在通俗拉丁语中转为阴性名词 forza，即法语 force 的来源。

items.en: Enforcier meant 'to strengthen, implant force into'; renforcier added the prefix re- 'again'. Force itself entered English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: enforcier 意为「加强、把力量注入其中」；renforcier 再添前缀 re-「再」。force 本身在十三世纪进入英语。

items.en: Reinforce appears in English in the fifteenth century, chiefly military: to reinforce a garrison is to send fresh men into it.
items.cn: reinforce 于十五世纪进入英语，主要用于军事：reinforce 一支驻军即向其增派新兵。

items.en: The building sense grows with reinforced concrete in the nineteenth century, and psychology adopts reinforcement in the twentieth for reward-shaped habits.
items.cn: 建筑义随十九世纪的钢筋混凝土成长；二十世纪心理学采用 reinforcement 指奖励塑造的习惯。

note.en: The first group gathers the fortis 'strong' family with its prefixes. The second group compares the verbs of making something stronger or firmer.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 fortis「强壮」词族及其各前缀。第二组比较「使更强、更稳」的动词。

entries.definition: the act of reinforcing, the extra material or troops sent, or the psychology term for reward.
entries.definitionCN: 加固行为、增派的兵力或材料，或心理学的「强化」。

entries.definition: strength, power, or a body of troops. It is the thing poured in by reinforce.
entries.definitionCN: 力；力量；部队。是 reinforce 所倾注之物。

entries.definition: to build strength in, especially walls and defences. It builds from scratch; reinforce adds to what stands.
entries.definitionCN: 设防；筑垒，尤指城墙防线。fortify 从头建强；reinforce 在既有之物上加固。

entries.definition: a fortified place, a stronghold. The strength turned into architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 要塞；堡垒。被凝固为建筑的力量。

entries.definition: an older spelling of reinforce, now rare; both forms meant the same pour of strength.
entries.definitionCN: reinforce 的旧式拼法，今已罕用；两形同义。

entries.definition: to make strong or stronger in any way. It is the general verb; reinforce implies adding something on top.
entries.definitionCN: 以任何方式使变强。是泛用动词；reinforce 隐含「在原有之上增添」。

entries.definition: to prop something weakening with supports. It props what is failing; reinforce prevents failure.
entries.definitionCN: 用支撑物顶住将倾之物。shore up 挽救衰败；reinforce 防患于未然。

entries.definition: to make firmer by combining or binding together. It joins parts; reinforce adds strength.
entries.definitionCN: 通过合并、凝聚使之稳固。consolidate 联结部分；reinforce 增添强度。

entries.definition: to support with a buttress, hence to back up an argument. It names the prop; reinforce names the pour.
entries.definitionCN: 以扶壁支撑，引申为支持论点。buttress 命名支撑物；reinforce 命名倾注。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: re- 'again' + en- 'in' + force 'strength', the family fortify, fortress, fort and effort, and the pouring-strength-into-a-wall picture.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：re-「再」+ en-「入」+ force「力」，词族 fortify、fortress、fort、effort，以及「往墙里灌注力量」的图景。

normal.en: The word is three real parts: re- again, en- into, force strength.
normal.cn: 这个词由三个真实部分构成：re-「再」、en-「入」、force「力」。

normal.en: Force came from Latin fortis, strong, the same root as fort, the stronghold.
normal.cn: force 出自拉丁语 fortis「强壮」，与 fort「要塞」同根。

normal.en: To reinforce is to pour strength into something again, as concrete is poured around steel bars.
normal.cn: reinforce 就是把力量再度注入某物，如混凝土浇在钢筋四周。

normal.en: The military sense is the oldest: reinforcements are fresh force poured into a battle.
normal.cn: 军事义最古老：增援就是注入战场的生力军。

normal.en: Habits are walls too: every reward poured in makes the behaviour harder to demolish.
normal.cn: 习惯也是墙：每灌进一次奖励，这个行为就更难拆除。

abstract.en: Picture an old wall with a new steel bar inside it: the wall is the same wall, only braver.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旧墙内多了一根新钢筋：墙还是那面墙，只是更硬气了。

abstract.en: Reinforce never replaces: it adds its weight to whatever already stands.
abstract.cn: reinforce 从不替换：它只是往已有之物上再添一份重量。

abstract.en: A repeated stereotype is a wall built by accident, one routine laugh at a time.
abstract.cn: 被反复强化的成见是一堵无意中砌成的墙，一次日常的笑砌一层。

examples.en: Engineers reinforced the old dam before the rainy season.
examples.cn: 工程师们在雨季前加固了旧堤坝。

examples.en: Her example reinforced my belief in second chances.
examples.cn: 她的经历强化了我对第二次机会的信念。

examples.en: The defenders asked for reinforcements before dawn.
examples.cn: 守军在黎明前请求增援。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「锐因福斯」——锐利的钢筋「因」「福」斯（混凝土）而让墙更牢 → reinforce 加固；强化（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自古法语 renforcier「再度加强」（re- 再 + enforcier 注入力量），force 上溯拉丁语 fortis「强壮的」，核心是「往既有之物里再灌注一份力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of reinforce, one pour seen in five places: walls, battle lines, arguments, habits, and prejudices nobody meant to build.
sensesIntro.cn: reinforce 的五个义项是同一次「倾注」落在五个地方：墙体、战线、论证、习惯，以及无人有意砌成的偏见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strength poured again into something that already stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：把力量再度灌入已经立在那里的东西。

chain: POUR IT INTO THE OLD WALL
SEND FRESH FORCE TO THE LINE

branches.en: MATERIALS: steel, concrete and timber poured into the structures we trust.
branches.cn: 材料：钢筋、混凝土与木料灌进我们信任的结构。

branches.en: BATTLE: fresh troops poured into a thinning line, the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 战场：把生力军灌进日渐单薄的防线，最古老的义项。

branches.en: ARGUMENTS: facts poured into a case until it can bear weight.
branches.cn: 论证：把事实灌进一个主张，直到它足以承重。

branches.en: MINDS: rewards and repetitions poured into habits and prejudices alike.
branches.cn: 心智：奖励与重复同样灌进习惯与偏见。

branches.en: ONE METHOD: whether the wall is concrete or behaviour, the pour is the same.
branches.cn: 同一方法：无论墙是混凝土还是行为，倾注的方式都一样。

intro.en: Reinforce stacks three morphemes: re- 'again', en- 'into', and force from Latin fortis 'strong'. The fortis family also gives fortify, fortress, fort, comfort and effort.
intro.cn: reinforce 叠加三个语素：re-「再」、en-「入」、force（出自拉丁语 fortis「强壮的」）。fortis 词族还给出 fortify、fortress、fort、comfort、effort。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is fortis 'strong', whose neuter plural fortia 'strengths' became the noun force in Romance. To reinforce is literally to put strength into again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 fortis「强壮的」，其中性复数 fortia「诸般力量」在罗曼语中转为名词 force。reinforce 的字面即「把力量再度放入」。

items.meaning: to pour strength in again; to strengthen
items.meaningCN: 加固；强化（re- 再 + en- 入 + force 力）

items.meaning: the act or result of reinforcing; extra troops; a reward in psychology

definition_en: a condition written into a law or contract, the act of supplying something, or a store of supplies kept for future use
core_image: 仓库里一袋袋粮食靠墙码好，门边贴着一张写明分配办法的纸
scene: 出发去山区之前，队长把面粉和罐头清点了一遍，又把分配办法写在纸上贴到门边。 The expedition carried enough provisions for two weeks in the mountains.

senses.title: A condition written into a law or contract
senses.definition: a condition or clause in a law, contract or agreement that states what must be done
senses.definitionCN: 法律、合同或协议中写明必须如何做的条件或条款
senses.example: A provision in the lease forbids keeping pets.
senses.exampleCN: 租约中有一条条款禁止养宠物。
senses.why: Latin provisio meant a seeing ahead, and a clause is exactly foresight written down: the parties decide now what will happen if something goes wrong later.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 provisio 意为「预先看见」，而条款正是被写下来的预见：各方在此刻就定好，以后出了某种情况该怎么办。

senses.title: The act of supplying something
senses.definition: the act of giving or supplying something, especially a service or a resource
senses.definitionCN: 给予或供应某物的行为，尤指服务或资源
senses.example: The provision of clean water is the city's first duty.
senses.exampleCN: 提供干净的饮用水是这座城市的首要职责。
senses.why: Once foresight turns into action, the action is supplying, and English uses the noun for the whole process of making something available.
senses.whyCN: 预见一旦化为行动，这个行动就是供应；英语用这个名词指「使某物可供使用」的整个过程。

senses.title: A store of supplies kept for future use
senses.definition: supplies of food, fuel or equipment kept ready, especially for a journey or an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 备好的食物、燃料或装备，尤指为旅途或应急准备的
senses.example: They laid in provisions before the snow closed the road.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在大雪封路之前备好了给养。
senses.why: What foresight produces is something set aside, so the noun shifts from the act of preparing to the goods sitting in the store room, usually in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 预见所产生的，就是被留出来的东西，于是这个名词从「准备的动作」转到「仓库里堆着的物资」，且常用复数。

senses.title: Preparation made in advance
senses.definition: arrangements made now so that a future need or risk is already taken care of
senses.definitionCN: 现在作出的安排，使将来的需求或风险已被照管到
senses.example: They made provision for their daughter's education years in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 他们多年前就为女儿的教育作了准备。
senses.why: This is the word at its closest to the Latin original: pure forethought, before anything has been handed over or stored.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最贴近拉丁原义的一层：纯粹的预先打算，还没有交出任何东西，也还没有囤起任何东西。

intro.en: Provision comes from a Latin noun of foresight built on the same verb as provide, and English borrowed the noun through French.
intro.cn: provision 来自一个表示「预见」的拉丁语名词，与 provide 建立在同一个动词上；英语是经法语借入这个名词的。

items.en: Videre meant to see, the plain visual root behind the whole family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，是整族词背后那个朴素的「看」的词根。

items.en: Providere meant to see ahead and to take care in advance, with pro- adding the forward direction.
items.cn: providere 意为往前看、提前照料，前缀 pro- 加上了「向前」的方向。

items.en: The noun provisio named the act of foreseeing and the care that followed from it; its stem provis- is what English kept.
items.cn: 名词 provisio 指预见这一动作以及随之而来的照料，英语保留的正是它的词干 provis-。

items.en: Old French provision carried the noun into the senses of supply and of a stipulated arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语 provision 把这个名词带到「供应」与「约定好的安排」这两层意思上。

items.en: Modern English uses the singular for a clause or the act of supplying, and the plural for goods stored up for a journey.
items.cn: 现代英语用单数指条款或供应的行为，用复数指为旅途囤起来的物资。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers words for clauses and for what is kept in store.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示条款与囤积之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to supply or to stipulate.
entries.definitionCN: 表示提供或规定的动词。

entries.definition: Arranged for the present only, to be changed later.
entries.definitionCN: 只为眼前安排的，以后会更改的。

entries.definition: Foresight and care, often seen as guidance from above.
entries.definitionCN: 远见与照料，常被视为来自上方的指引。

entries.definition: Careful about the future, especially with money.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来打算的，尤指用钱谨慎的。

entries.definition: A single condition in a legal document.
entries.definitionCN: 法律文件中的单项条件。

entries.definition: An amount of something available for use.

entries.definition: Goods kept in store for future use.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来使用而存着的货物。

entries.definition: A condition that must be met in an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 协议中必须满足的条件。

normalIntro.en: The word is foresight that has cooled into an object, and its memories sit on the Latin stem, on the written clause and on the plural in the store room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是冷却成实物的预见，记忆点落在拉丁词干、写下的条款，以及仓库里的复数形式上。

normal.en: Provision and provide share the Latin verb providere, but the noun came through French while the verb came by another route, which is why the vowel changed.
normal.cn: provision 与 provide 共享拉丁语动词 providere，但名词经法语传来，动词走的是另一条路，所以元音变了。

normal.en: Provis- is the stem of Latin provisio, so the -sion ending was not added in English.
normal.cn: provis- 是拉丁语 provisio 的词干，所以 -sion 并不是英语后来加上的后缀。

normal.en: Provisional keeps the idea of something arranged in advance and adds the hint that the arrangement is only for now.
normal.cn: provisional 保留「事先安排」的意思，并加上「这个安排只管眼前」的意味。

normal.en: In contracts the word means a clause, because a clause is a piece of written foresight.
normal.cn: 在合同里这个词指条款，因为条款就是一段写下来的预见。

normal.en: The plural provisions almost always means food and equipment for a journey, not several clauses.
normal.cn: 复数 provisions 几乎总指旅途所需的食物和装备，而不是好几条条款。

abstract.en: Provision is foresight that has cooled into an object: a clause on paper or a sack in the store room.
abstract.cn: provision 是冷却成实物的预见：要么是纸上的一条条款，要么是仓库里的一袋粮食。

abstract.en: Every contract is a small machine for the future, and its provisions are the parts.
abstract.cn: 每份合同都是一台为未来造的小机器，条款就是它的零件。

abstract.en: To make provision is to admit that the future will ask for something you do not yet need.
abstract.cn: 作出准备，就是承认未来会来索要你此刻还不需要的东西。

definition_zh: 精确的；准确的；明确的；严谨的；恰好的
definition_en: exact and accurate in detail; clearly defined and not approximate; careful about details
core_image: 一刀切下去，边缘干净，不多不少
scene: 这台仪器能把温度测到十分之一个刻度。 The instrument can measure temperature to a precise tenth of a degree.
sceneCN: 这里 precise 是「精确到很小单位」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这台仪器能把温度测量到十分之一度的精确度。场景要点：刻度细、读数明确、没有模糊区间；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 精确的；准确的；明确的；严谨的

derivatives.zh: 精确；精密；精度
精确地；恰恰；正是
精确；严谨
