senses.title: Exact in measurement
senses.titleCN: 精确的：读数细到很小一格
senses.definition: exact and accurate, with details measured or stated to a fine degree
senses.definitionCN: 精确而准确，细节被测量或陈述到很细的程度
senses.example: The instrument can measure temperature to a precise tenth of a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器能把温度测量到十分之一度的精确度。
senses.why: Latin praecidere means to cut off. A precise measurement is one cut cleanly, with no ragged margin of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecidere 意为“切掉”。精确的测量就是切得干净，边缘没有参差的疑问。

senses.title: Clearly defined and distinct
senses.definition: clearly stated or defined, so that there is no ambiguity
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或界定清楚，因而没有歧义
senses.example: The contract gives a precise definition of the delivery date.
senses.exampleCN: 合同对交付日期给出了明确的定义。
senses.why: If the edges are cut cleanly, the shape is unambiguous. A precise definition has no fuzzy border where other things could slip in.
senses.whyCN: 边缘切得干净，形状就不含糊。明确的定义没有模糊的边界，别的东西无从混入。

senses.title: Careful about small details
senses.titleCN: 严谨的：在小处也不放过
senses.definition: careful and exact in doing or describing something, paying attention to small details
senses.definitionCN: 在做或描述某事时仔细准确，注意细小之处
senses.example: She is precise about the order of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她对步骤的先后十分严谨。
senses.why: The cut-clean image becomes a habit of mind: refusing to let any detail stay rough.
senses.whyCN: “切得干净”的画面变成一种思维习惯：不允许任何细节保持粗糙。

senses.title: Strict about rules or standards
senses.titleCN: 讲究的：按规矩来，不将就
senses.definition: strict and particular about how things are done, often in matters of form
senses.definitionCN: 对做事方式严格挑剔，常指形式与礼数方面
senses.example: He was precise in his dress and punctual to the minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他衣着讲究，并且准时到分钟。
senses.why: A person who cuts every edge cleanly can become a person who insists on exact form. The trait shifts from result to temperament.
senses.whyCN: 一个把每条边都切干净的人，可能变成坚持确切形式的人。这个特征从结果转到了性情。

senses.title: Emphatic: the very same
senses.definition: used to emphasize that a particular thing or moment is exactly the one meant
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调所说的正是那一个事物或那一刻
senses.example: At that precise moment, the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 正是在那一刻，灯灭了。
senses.why: An exact point has no width. Using precise here says the moment cannot be widened into a general period.
senses.whyCN: 一个精确的点没有宽度。这里用 precise，是说那一刻无法被放宽成一段笼统的时期。

senses.title: Technical: high precision
senses.titleCN: 精密的：仪器能做到极细刻度
senses.definition: of an instrument or method, able to produce very exact results
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器或方法能给出非常精确的结果
senses.example: Precise instruments are required for this experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验需要精密的仪器。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the tool that makes the clean cut. Precision becomes a property of the instrument, not only of the number.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词贴到了做出干净切割的工具上。精确性成了仪器的属性，而不只是数字的属性。

senses.title: Discourse: to be exact
senses.definition: in the phrase to be precise, used to correct or narrow what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 在 to be precise 这一短语中，用来修正或收窄刚才说过的话
senses.example: He arrived late, at ten past eight, to be precise.
senses.exampleCN: 他到得晚了，确切地说是八点十分。
senses.why: The speaker performs the cutting in speech: trimming a rough statement down to its exact edge.
senses.whyCN: 说话人在言语里执行这一刀：把粗略的说法修到确切的边缘。

senses.title: Neatly executed in movement or art
senses.titleCN: 动作精准：每一笔每一动都不含糊
senses.definition: performed with exact control, as in dance, surgery, or drawing
senses.definitionCN: 以精确的控制完成，如舞蹈、手术或绘画中的动作
senses.example: The dancer's precise movements made the whole phrase look effortless.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者精准的动作让整个乐句显得毫不费力。
senses.why: The body can cut cleanly too. Precision in movement is the same refusal of slack, expressed in muscle.
senses.whyCN: 身体也能切得干净。动作的精准是同一种对松弛的拒绝，只是用肌肉表达出来。

intro.en: Precise comes from a Latin participle meaning cut off. The path from 'cut short' to 'exact' is the story of a metaphor that became a standard.
intro.cn: precise 来自一个意为“被切掉”的拉丁分词。从“切短”到“精确”的路径，是一个比喻变成标准的历程。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Here it intensifies rather than marks time: the cutting is done right at the front edge.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。这里它起加强作用而非标时间：这一刀正切在前沿上。

items.en: Caedere meant 'to cut, to strike'. English gets scissors, decide, concise, and circumcise from this family.
items.cn: caedere 意为“切、砍”。英语的 scissors、decide、concise、circumcise 都出自这个词族。

items.en: Praecidere meant 'to cut off, to cut short'. It described trimming something down to a clean limit.
items.cn: praecidere 意为“切掉、切短”。它描述把某物修到干净的界限。

items.en: The past participle praecisus meant 'cut off, shortened'. It is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 praecisus 意为“被切掉的、被缩短的”。它是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: French used précis for 'cut short, concise, exact'. English borrowed the form in the 16th century.
items.cn: 法语用 précis 表示“切短的、简洁的、确切的”。英语在 16 世纪借入这个词形。

items.en: The sense moves from 'cut short' to 'definite' and then to 'accurate to a fine degree'. Modern usage applies it to numbers, definitions, instruments, people, and moments.
items.cn: 词义从“切短”转到“确定”，再转到“精确到很细的程度”。现代用法把它用于数字、定义、仪器、人以及时刻。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for cutting. The second group collects words for accuracy and exactness.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“切”的动词。第二组收表示准确与确切的词。

entries.definition: the quality of being exact, or the degree of exactness. It is the noun built on precise.
entries.definitionCN: 精确的性质，或精确的程度。它是建立在 precise 之上的名词。

entries.definition: exactly, or used to confirm a statement. Precisely can answer a question with a firm yes.
entries.definitionCN: 精确地，或用于确认某陈述。precisely 可以以干脆的“正是”来回答提问。

entries.definition: brief and clear. Con- 'together' plus caedere 'cut': cut down to essentials.
entries.definitionCN: 简短而清楚。con-“一起”加 caedere“切”：切到只剩要点。

entries.definition: to settle a question. De- 'off' plus caedere 'cut': cut off alternatives until one remains.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题定下来。de-“去掉”加 caedere“切”：切掉其他选项，直到只剩一个。

entries.definition: correct in every detail. Exact stresses correctness; precise stresses fine definition and care.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都正确。exact 强调正确；precise 强调界定细密与讲究。

entries.definition: correct and free from error. Accurate is about truth to fact; precise is about narrowness of specification.
entries.definitionCN: 正确且无错误。accurate 关乎与事实相符；precise 关乎规格的窄细。

entries.definition: clearly identified rather than general. Specific names the thing; precise describes how finely it is defined.
entries.definitionCN: 明确指出的，而非笼统的。specific 指名的是哪一个；precise 描述界定得多细。

entries.definition: showing great attention to detail. Meticulous fits sense 03 and stresses care rather than measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 对细节极为注意。meticulous 对应第 3 义项，强调用心而非测量。

entries.definition: clear and not uncertain. Definite fits sense 02 and is close to the 'cut clean' image.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而不含糊。definite 对应第 2 义项，贴近“切得干净”的画面。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the clean cut, the narrow definition, the meticulous person, the exact instant, and the phrase to be precise.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：干净的一刀、窄而清楚的定义、一丝不苟的人、正好的那一刻、以及 to be precise 这句话。

normal.en: Precise comes from a verb meaning to cut off. Picture a knife trimming away every loose edge.
normal.cn: precise 来自意为“切掉”的动词。想象一把刀把每一条松散的边都修掉。

normal.en: A precise definition has a clean border: nothing else can slip in.
normal.cn: 明确的定义有一条干净的边界：别的东西混不进来。

normal.en: Precise instruments are the ones whose readings do not wobble.
normal.cn: 精密的仪器，就是读数不会晃的那种。

normal.en: At that precise moment means the moment has no width; you cannot widen it into an afternoon.
normal.cn: at that precise moment 意为那一刻没有宽度，你不能把它放宽成一个下午。

normal.en: To be precise is to take the rough sentence and trim it to its exact edge.
normal.cn: to be precise 就是把粗糙的句子修到确切的边缘。

abstract.en: Precision is a relation between a statement and a tolerance, not a property of the world by itself.
abstract.cn: 精确是陈述与容许误差之间的关系，不是世界本身的属性。

abstract.en: Every precise definition is also an exclusion: to say exactly what it is, is to say what it is not.
abstract.cn: 每个明确的定义同时也是一次排除：说清它是什么，就是说清它不是什么。

abstract.en: The same cut that makes a thing exact can make it narrow; precision always trades scope for edge.
abstract.cn: 使事物精确的那一刀，也可能使它变窄；精确总是用范围换取边缘。

examples.en: The instructions were precise enough that a beginner could follow them.
examples.cn: 这些指示足够精确，初学者也能照着做。

examples.en: To be precise, the meeting lasted forty-two minutes.
examples.cn: 确切地说，会议持续了四十二分钟。

examples.en: Her precise handwriting filled the margins without a single correction.
examples.cn: 她精准的字迹填满了页边，没有一处涂改。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞赛斯”——普瑞在赛前把秒表按到千分之一秒，就是 precise（精确的）

root: 拉丁语 praecidere“切掉、切短”（prae“在前”+ caedere“切”）的过去分词 praecisus → 法语 précis → 英语 precise（16 世纪）；与 concise、decide、scissors 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a clean cut. A clean cut gives exact numbers, unambiguous definitions, meticulous habits, and instruments that do not wobble. The emphatic use fixes one instant, and to be precise performs the same trimming in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是干净的一刀。干净的一刀给出精确的数字、不含糊的定义、一丝不苟的习惯，以及不晃的仪器。强调用法固定住某一刻，而 to be precise 是在言语里执行同一番修边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade trimming an edge until nothing rough is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃修边，直到不剩一点毛糙。

branches.en: MEASURE: exact readings and the instruments that produce them.
branches.cn: 测量：精确的读数，以及产生这些读数的仪器。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: a definition with a clean edge, and a moment with no width.
branches.cn: 边界：边缘干净的定义，以及没有宽度的时刻。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: the meticulous person and the person strict about form.
branches.cn: 性情：一丝不苟的人，以及讲究形式的人。

branches.en: SPEECH: trimming a rough statement down to the exact word.
branches.cn: 言语：把粗略的说法修到确切的字眼。

branches.en: MOVEMENT: the same clean edge performed by the body.
branches.cn: 动作：由身体执行的同一种干净边缘。

intro.en: Precise is one participle from the cut family. The same verb, with different prefixes, gives concise, decide, and scissors.
intro.cn: precise 是“切”词族里的一个分词。同一个动词配上不同前缀，给出 concise、decide、scissors。

latinIntro.en: Latin praecisus reached English through French précis, which is why the English form lacks the Latin -us ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praecisus 经法语 précis 到达英语，所以英语形式没有拉丁的 -us 词尾。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 数量；量；大量；数学量；（语音）音长
definition_en: an amount that can be counted or measured; a large amount of something; a measurable property studied in mathematics and physics; the length of a sound in speech
core_image: 一排贴着编号的粮袋，袋口露出不同的刻度线
scene: 仓库管理员拿着清单，一袋一袋核对面粉的重量和袋数，记下每一行的差额。 A large quantity of flour was stored in the warehouse that winter.
sceneCN: 这里 quantity 是「大量」（第 2 个义项：不指具体数目，只强调量大）；句意为那个冬天仓库里存了大量面粉。画面里可留意：清单、粮袋、墙上的刻度。

pos.zh: 数量；量；大量；数学量；音长

collocations.zh: 未知量；难以预料的人或事

derivatives.zh: quantity 换后缀成动词，指用数字确定数量
quantity 加 -itative，指「定量的、与数量有关的」
quantify 加 -er，指表示数量的词，如 many、some

senses.title: An amount that can be counted or measured
senses.definition: the amount of something, especially when it can be counted or measured
senses.definitionCN: 某物的量，尤其是可以被清点或计量的部分
senses.example: The quantity of water in the tank fell overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 水箱里的水量一夜之间减少了。
senses.why: Latin quantitas answered the question how much, so the noun first names any measurable amount.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quantitas 回答的是「多少」这个问题，因此这个名词首先指任何可计量的量。

senses.title: A large amount
senses.definition: a great amount of something, used without a number
senses.definitionCN: 某物很大的量，不与具体数字连用
senses.example: They bought paper in quantity to save money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们大量买纸以省钱。
senses.why: Once the noun meant amount in general, the bare word could stand for a big amount, especially in the phrase in quantity.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既泛指「量」，光秃秃的单词就能表示「大量」，尤其在 in quantity 这一说法里。

senses.title: A measurable property in mathematics
senses.definition: a property such as mass, length or force that can be measured and expressed by a number
senses.definitionCN: 质量、长度或力这类可以被测量并用数字表示的性质
senses.example: Force is a vector quantity, while mass is a scalar quantity.
senses.exampleCN: 力是矢量量，而质量是标量量。
senses.why: Science needed a neutral noun for anything measurable, and borrowed the everyday word for amount.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个中性的名词来指任何可测量之物，于是借用了日常表示「量」的词。

senses.title: The length of a speech sound
senses.definition: the relative length of a vowel or syllable, which can carry meaning in some languages
senses.definitionCN: 元音或音节的相对长短，在某些语言中可以区别意义
senses.example: Latin poetry depends on the quantity of each syllable, not on stress.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语诗歌依靠每个音节的长短，而不是依靠重音。
senses.why: In phonetics the amount of time a sound lasts is simply its quantity, the same notion of amount applied to time.
senses.whyCN: 在语音学里，一个声音持续的时间长短就是它的 quantity，仍是「量」这一概念被用在时间上。

intro.en: Quantity comes from the Latin question word for how much and the noun built on it, passed through French into English.
intro.cn: quantity 源自拉丁语表示「多少」的疑问词及由它构成的名词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quantus was the question word for how much or how great, the partner of qualis for of what kind.
items.cn: quantus 是表示「多少、多大」的疑问词，与表示「何种」的 qualis 是一对搭档。

items.en: Quantitas was coined as the noun for the answer, naming size or amount as opposed to kind.
items.cn: quantitas 是为回答而造的名词，指大小或多少，与「种类」相对。

items.en: Old French quantite kept the sense of amount and also served for the length of a sound in grammar.
items.cn: 古法语 quantite 保留了「量」的意思，在语法中也用来指音的长短。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the French form and later remade the spelling after the Latin noun.
items.cn: 中古英语借入法语形式，后来又照着拉丁名词改写了拼写。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for plain amounts, for large amounts, for measurable properties and for sound length.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指普通数量、大量、可测的量以及语音的长短。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the Latin stem of how much; the near-meaning group collects nouns of amount, number and size.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「多少」词干上的形式；近义组收表示数量、数目与规模的名词。

entries.definition: To express something as a number or an amount.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物用数字或数量表示出来。

entries.definition: Measured by amount rather than by kind.
entries.definitionCN: 按数量而非按性质衡量的。

entries.definition: A word such as many or some that shows amount.
entries.definitionCN: 表示数量的词，如 many 或 some。

entries.definition: A fixed smallest unit of energy in physics.
entries.definitionCN: 物理学中一份固定的最小能量单位。

entries.definition: How much there is of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物有多少。

entries.definition: A count of separate things.
entries.definitionCN: 对可分离事物的计数。

entries.definition: The amount of space something fills.
entries.definitionCN: 某物占据的空间大小。

entries.definition: A total reached by adding amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 把数量相加得到的总数。

normalIntro.en: The word answers how much, in contrast with quality, which answers what kind; the pair has been a matched set since Latin.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词回答「多少」，与回答「何种」的 quality 相对；这对词从拉丁语起就是一套。

normal.en: Quantity and quality are a matched pair: one asks how much, the other asks what kind.
normal.cn: quantity 与 quality 是一对搭档：一个问多少，一个问何种。

normal.en: Quantify means to turn something into a quantity, to give it a number.
normal.cn: quantify 意为把某物变成数量，也就是给它一个数字。

normal.en: Buying in quantity means buying a large amount at one time, which usually lowers the price.
normal.cn: in quantity 指一次买很大的量，通常能压低价格。

normal.en: In physics a vector quantity has direction, while a scalar quantity has only size.
normal.cn: 物理中矢量量有方向，而标量量只有大小。

normal.en: In Latin verse, quantity tells you how long each syllable lasts, and that decides the rhythm.
normal.cn: 在拉丁诗里，音长告诉你每个音节持续多久，由此决定节奏。

abstract.en: Every number hides a decision about what counts as one unit, so quantity is never purely natural.
abstract.cn: 每个数字都藏着「什么算作一个单位」的决定，所以数量从来不纯是自然的。

abstract.en: A large quantity can feel like abundance and also like a burden, depending on who must carry it.
abstract.cn: 大量的东西既能像富足，也能像负担，取决于由谁来扛。

abstract.en: Quantity promises fairness by counting, yet counting always leaves out what cannot be counted.
abstract.cn: 数量靠清点来许诺公平，可清点总会漏掉无法清点的东西。

examples.en: The recipe needs only a small quantity of salt.
examples.cn: 这道菜只需要少量的盐。

examples.en: Books of this kind are cheaper when bought in quantity.
examples.cn: 这类书批量购买时更便宜。

examples.en: Speed is a scalar quantity, but velocity is a vector quantity.
examples.cn: 速率是标量量，而速度是矢量量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「框特体」——用框子一框，量出这一堆东西的体量，记住 quantity 是数量、量。

root: 拉丁语 quantus（多少）→ quantitas（数量）→ 古法语 quantite → 英语 quantity；同族有 quantify、quantitative、quantum。

sensesIntro.en: The core is how much there is; the senses move from any amount to a large amount, then to a measured property in science and to the length of a sound.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「有多少」；义项从任何数量走向大量，再走向科学中可测的量与语音的长短。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of numbered grain sacks, each cut open at a different mark on a measuring stick.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排贴着编号的粮袋，每袋都在量尺的不同刻度处被割开。

branches.en: a tank marked with a water line
branches.cn: 水箱上标着的一道水线

branches.en: a cart loaded until the boards bend
branches.cn: 装到木板发弯的一车货物

branches.en: an arrow with length and direction
branches.cn: 一支有长度也有方向的箭头

branches.en: a syllable held longer than its neighbour
branches.cn: 比相邻音节拖得更长的一个音节

branches.en: the same act of measuring, once in a kitchen and once in a lab
branches.cn: 同一个测量动作，一次在厨房，一次在实验室

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin question of how much and the noun suffix that turns an answer into a thing that can be handled.
intro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁语「多少」这一问，以及把答案变成可把握之物的名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin left a small family around quantus, the partner of qualis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语围绕 quantus 留下了一个小词群，它与 qualis 互为搭档。

definition_zh: 次要的；中学的；第二位的；继发的
definition_en: less important than something else, relating to secondary school, coming second in order, or resulting from something else
core_image: 主干道旁的分岔小路，路口立着一块不起眼的小牌子
scene: 主路堵得水泄不通，他拐进一条次要的小路。 He took a secondary road to avoid the traffic.
sceneCN: 这里 secondary 是「次要的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他走一条次要道路以避开拥堵。

derivatives.zh: 第二的
其次
次要地
次要性

senses.title: Less important
senses.definition: less important than the main thing
senses.definitionCN: 不如主要事物重要
senses.example: Safety is never a secondary concern.
senses.exampleCN: 安全从来都不是次要问题。
senses.why: This is the broad everyday sense of lower priority.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示优先级较低的宽泛日常义。

senses.title: Of secondary school
senses.definition: relating to education for older children
senses.definitionCN: 与较大儿童的教育有关
senses.example: She teaches at a secondary school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所中学教书。
senses.why: The school level comes after primary education.
senses.whyCN: 中学阶段在小学教育之后。

senses.title: Coming second
senses.definition: second in order, rank, or level
senses.definitionCN: 在顺序、等级或层次上居第二
senses.example: The report relied on secondary sources.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告依赖二手资料。
senses.why: A second-hand source is one step from the original.
senses.whyCN: 二手资料与原初来源隔了一步。

senses.title: Resulting from something
senses.definition: caused by or developing from an earlier condition
senses.definitionCN: 由先前状况引起或由此发展而来
senses.example: The doctor treated a secondary infection.
senses.exampleCN: 医生治疗了继发感染。
senses.why: Medical use names a condition that follows another.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法指紧随另一状况出现的病症。

intro.en: Secondary comes from Latin secundarius, from secundus, following or second.
intro.cn: secondary 源自拉丁语 secundarius，出自 secundus（跟随的、第二的）。

items.en: Secundus meant following or second.
items.cn: secundus 意为跟随的或第二的。

items.en: Secundarius meant of the second rank.
items.cn: secundarius 意为第二等级的。

items.en: Secondary entered English as a word for second rank.
items.cn: secondary 以「第二等级」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word described subordinate things and school levels.
items.cn: 该词用来形容从属事物与学校阶段。

items.en: Medicine added the sense of a following condition.
items.cn: 医学又增加了「继发状况」的义项。

note.en: Secondary is compared with similar-looking words and with words for lesser importance.
note.cn: 把 secondary 与形近词以及表示较次要的词作比较。

entries.definition: coming after the first
entries.definitionCN: 第二的

entries.definition: as a second point
entries.definitionCN: 其次

entries.definition: a person who keeps records
entries.definitionCN: 秘书

entries.definition: small or not very important
entries.definitionCN: 次要的；较小的

entries.definition: not as great or important
entries.definitionCN: 较次要的

entries.definition: lower in rank or importance
entries.definitionCN: 从属的

normalIntro.en: Secondary means second in importance, level, or origin.
normalIntro.cn: secondary 意为在重要性、层级或来源上居第二。

normal.en: Secondary school follows primary school.
normal.cn: secondary school 是小学之后的中学。

normal.en: A secondary source is not the original.
normal.cn: secondary source 不是原始资料。

normal.en: Secondary means less important, not useless.
normal.cn: secondary 表示较次要，而非毫无用处。

normal.en: A secondary infection follows the first one.
normal.cn: secondary infection 是继发于初次感染的。

normal.en: Secondary shares its root with second.
normal.cn: secondary 与 second 同根。

abstract.en: Calling something secondary is a way of ranking the world.
abstract.cn: 称某事为次要，是在给世界排位。

abstract.en: What is secondary can still decide the outcome.
abstract.cn: 次要因素有时仍能决定结果。

abstract.en: Every first needs a second to follow it.
abstract.cn: 每一个第一都需要一个跟随的第二。

examples.en: Safety is never a secondary concern.
examples.cn: 安全从来都不是次要问题。

examples.en: She teaches at a secondary school.
examples.cn: 她在一所中学教书。

examples.en: The report relied on secondary sources.
examples.cn: 这份报告依赖二手资料。

dict_mnemonic.text: secondary 由 second（第二）加形容词后缀 -ary 构成，表示「排在第二位的、次要的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 secundarius（第二等级的），出自 secundus（第二），核心义「居其次的」。

sensesIntro.en: Secondary means less important, relating to secondary school, second in rank, or following another condition.
sensesIntro.cn: secondary 意为次要的、中学的、第二位的，或继发的。

core.en: Something that follows and ranks below a first.
core.cn: 跟随在第一之后、等级较低的事物。

branches.en: A matter of lower priority.
branches.cn: 优先级较低的事项。

branches.en: The school level after primary.
branches.cn: 小学之后的学校阶段。

branches.en: A rank or source one step from the first.
branches.cn: 距第一等一步之遥的等级或来源。

branches.en: A condition that follows another.
branches.cn: 紧随另一状况出现的病症。

branches.en: Lower importance and second rank often mean the same.
branches.cn: 较低重要性与第二等级常常是同一回事。

intro.en: Secondary builds on second, with words for order and priority.
intro.cn: secondary 以 second 为基础，构成表示顺序与优先级的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin secundus and secundarius are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secundus 与 secundarius 是历史词根。

items.example: He finished second in the race.
items.exampleCN: 他在比赛中获得第二名。

items.meaning: second helpings or units of time
items.example: The clock ticked away the seconds.

items.exampleCN: 其次，我们需要更多时间。

items.example: The fund is used primarily, not secondarily.
items.exampleCN: 这笔资金用于主要用途，而非次要用途。

items.example: The secondariness of the issue was clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题的次要性很清楚。

items.example: They settled for a second-best option.
The parcel went by second-class mail.

definition_zh: 追赶；追求；追逐
definition_en: to run after a person or animal in order to catch them, or to try hard to obtain something
core_image: 一个人沿着地上的脚印拼命奔跑
scene: 狗从院门冲出去追一只野兔。 The dog chased a rabbit across the field.
sceneCN: 这里 chase 指「追赶」（第 1 个义项：追着某人或某物跑）；句意是狗追着一只野兔跑过田野。

derivatives.zh: 追逐者；追赶的人
追逐；追猎

senses.title: To run after someone
senses.definition: to run after a person or animal in order to catch them
senses.definitionCN: 追在人或动物后面以便抓住
senses.example: The dog chased a rabbit across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 狗追着一只野兔跑过田野。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to try to seize, and running after prey is that attempt in motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为试图抓住，追着猎物跑正是这种企图在移动。

senses.title: To try to obtain something
senses.definition: to try hard to get something such as money, success or a person
senses.definitionCN: 努力获得金钱、成功或某个人
senses.example: He spent years chasing a dream.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了多年追求一个梦想。
senses.why: The hunt for prey became a hunt for goals that cannot be caught by hand.
senses.whyCN: 对猎物的追捕，变成了对手无法用手抓住的目标的追逐。

senses.title: An act of pursuing
senses.definition: the act of running after someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 追在某人或某物后面的行为
senses.example: The police gave up the chase.
senses.exampleCN: 警方放弃了追逐。
senses.why: The verb's action turned into a noun, so the pursuit itself became a chase.
senses.whyCN: 动词的动作转成名词，追逐本身便成了一个 chase。

intro.en: Chase comes from a Latin verb of trying to seize, through Old French chacier.
intro.cn: chase 源自拉丁语表示试图抓住的动词，经古法语 chacier 传来。

items.en: Captare meant to try to catch or seize.
items.cn: 拉丁语 captare 意为试图抓住或夺取。

items.en: Captiare carried the hunting sense into popular speech.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 captiare 把追猎义带入日常口语。

items.en: Chacier meant to hunt or drive away.
items.cn: chacier 意为追猎或赶走。

items.en: English chase first meant to hunt animals.
items.cn: 英语 chase 最初指追猎动物。

items.en: The word now covers car chases and the pursuit of aims.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖汽车追逐与对目标的追求。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chase stem, while the meaning group lists pursuing verbs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chase 词干，近义组列出追捕类动词。

entries.definition: a person or thing that chases
entries.definitionCN: 追赶的人或物

entries.definition: the act of running after
entries.definitionCN: 追赶的行为

entries.definition: more than one chase
entries.definitionCN: 追逐的复数形式

entries.definition: to follow in order to catch
entries.definitionCN: 跟随以便抓住

entries.definition: to chase animals for food
entries.definitionCN: 为食物而追猎动物

entries.definition: to go after someone
entries.definitionCN: 跟在某人后面

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the seize root, the car chase phrase and the pursuit of a dream.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「抓住」词根、短语 car chase 以及追梦义。

normal.en: Chase and catch share an old idea of seizing, since one leads to the other.
normal.cn: chase 与 catch 共享古老的「抓住」之意，因为前者通向后者。

normal.en: Chase after is the phrase for both a runaway dog and a distant goal.
normal.cn: chase after 既用于跑掉的狗，也用于遥远的目标。

normal.en: Give chase means to start running after, not to hand something over.
normal.cn: give chase 意为开始追赶，而不是把东西交出去。

normal.en: Chase away reverses the direction and means to drive off.
normal.cn: chase away 把方向反过来，意为赶走。

normal.en: A car chase fills the screen with motion and noise.
normal.cn: car chase 用动作与噪声填满银幕。

abstract.en: Picture a dog cutting a straight line through tall grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗在深草中划出一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a runner reaching for a finish line that keeps moving.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者伸手去够一条不断移动的终点线。

abstract.en: Picture two cars flashing through a wet tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象两辆车在潮湿的隧道里飞驰。

examples.en: The cat chased the ball under the sofa.
examples.cn: 猫把球追到了沙发底下。

examples.en: Reporters chased the story for weeks.
examples.cn: 记者追这条新闻追了好几周。

examples.en: He gave up the chase after two blocks.
examples.cn: 他追了两条街就放弃了。

dict_mnemonic.text: chase 与 catch 同源感：追（chase）的最终目的，就是抓（catch）到。

root: 源自拉丁语 captare（试图抓住），经晚期拉丁语 captiare 与古法语 chacier 进入英语；与 catch 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Trying to seize gives the physical pursuit, then the pursuit of aims, then the name of the pursuit itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 试图抓住先给出身体上的追赶，再给出对目标的追求，最后给出追逐这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner closing in on prey.
core.cn: 核心意象：奔跑者逐渐逼近猎物。

branches.en: A dog chases a rabbit to catch it.
branches.cn: 狗追野兔是为了抓住它。

branches.en: A dream is chased without any physical prey.
branches.cn: 追梦并没有实体的猎物。

branches.en: The chase itself becomes a thing to name.
branches.cn: 追逐本身成了一个可以被命名的东西。

branches.en: The verb and noun describe one continuous action.
branches.cn: 动词与名词描述同一个连续动作。

branches.en: Prey and goals are both things to run after.
branches.cn: 猎物与目标都是要追的东西。

intro.en: Chase forms chaser and chasing, and the collocation chase away reverses the direction.
intro.cn: chase 构成 chaser 与 chasing，搭配 chase away 则把方向反过来。

latinIntro.en: Latin captare is the seizing verb behind chase and catch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 captare 是 chase 与 catch 背后的「抓取」动词。

items.example: The film has two long chases.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影有两段长长的追逐戏。

items.example: Captare is the old hunting verb.
items.exampleCN: captare 是古老的追猎动词。

items.meaning: to follow in order to reach
items.exampleCN: 他们继续推进这个计划。

latinEntries.exampleCN: chacier 以 chase 进入英语。

definition_zh: 支出；经费；消耗
definition_en: the amount of money spent; the act of spending money; the use of time or energy
core_image: 一笔钱被称量后付出去
scene: 政府计划削减明年的公共开支。 The government plans to cut public expenditure next year.
sceneCN: 这里 expenditure 是「支出、经费」（第 1 个义项）；句意：政府计划削减明年的公共开支。

derivatives.zh: 花费；消耗
费用；开支
可消耗的；可牺牲的

senses.title: Money spent
senses.definition: the amount of money that is spent
senses.definitionCN: 花出去的钱的总额
senses.example: Public expenditure rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年公共开支大幅上升。
senses.why: The noun names money paid out.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指付出去的钱。

senses.title: Budget item
senses.definition: a particular sum of money used for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一用途拨出的一笔钱
senses.example: The school increased its expenditure on books.
senses.exampleCN: 学校增加了购书经费。
senses.why: Money paid out is organized into budget items.
senses.whyCN: 支出的钱被归入预算项目。

senses.title: Use of energy
senses.definition: the use of time, energy, or effort
senses.definitionCN: 时间、精力或努力的使用
senses.example: The project required a huge expenditure of energy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目需要消耗巨大的精力。
senses.why: Spending extends from money to effort.
senses.whyCN: 「花费」从金钱扩展到精力。

intro.en: Expenditure comes from Latin expendere, to weigh out and pay.
intro.cn: expenditure 源自拉丁语 expendere，意为「称量后付出」。

items.en: Expendere means to weigh out and pay.
items.cn: expendere 意为称量后支付。

items.en: It joins ex- (out) with pendere (to weigh).
items.cn: 它由 ex-（向外）与 pendere（称量）构成。

items.en: Expenditura names money paid out.
items.cn: expenditura 指付出去的钱。

items.en: Expenditure is used in accounts.
items.cn: expenditure 出现在账目用语中。

items.en: Expenditure covers money and energy used.
items.cn: expenditure 涵盖花掉的钱与消耗的精力。

items.en: Public expenditure is a common phrase.
items.cn: public expenditure 成为常用搭配。

note.en: Expenditure is money paid out; an expedition is a journey.
note.cn: expenditure 是支出，expedition 则是远征。

entries.definition: able to be used up or sacrificed
entries.definitionCN: 可消耗的；可牺牲的

entries.definition: an organized journey
entries.definitionCN: 探险；远征

entries.definition: the state of being uncovered
entries.definitionCN: 暴露；曝光

entries.definition: money that is spent
entries.definitionCN: 开销；支出

entries.definition: the amount paid for something
entries.definitionCN: 成本；花费

entries.definition: money spent on a project
entries.definitionCN: 支出；经费

normalIntro.en: Expenditure is the money or energy you pay out.
normalIntro.cn: expenditure 就是你付出去的钱或精力。

normal.en: The city reduced expenditure on new roads.
normal.cn: 市里削减了新修道路的开支。

normal.en: Capital expenditure rose with the new factory.
normal.cn: 随着新工厂建设，资本支出上升。

normal.en: They kept a record of every expenditure.
normal.cn: 他们记录每一笔支出。

normal.en: The rescue needed a great expenditure of effort.
normal.cn: 那次救援耗费了巨大的努力。

normal.en: Health expenditure takes a large share of the budget.
normal.cn: 医疗开支占预算的很大一部分。

abstract.en: Picture coins weighed on a small scale.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币在小秤上被称量。

abstract.en: Imagine a ledger with columns of payments.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记满付款栏目的账簿。

abstract.en: Think of energy pouring out like water.
abstract.cn: 想象精力像水一样流出去。

examples.en: The report tracks government expenditure each year.
examples.cn: 这份报告追踪每年的政府开支。

examples.en: They argued about the expenditure on the new bridge.
examples.cn: 他们为修建新桥的开支争论不休。

examples.en: The task demanded a large expenditure of time.
examples.cn: 这项任务需要投入大量时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「expenditure」里有 expend（花费）：把钱包里的钱向外称出去，就是「支出」。

root: 拉丁语 expendere（称量后支付）由 ex-（向外）与 pendere（称量）构成，核心义「把钱称出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Expenditure means money spent, a budget item, or the use of time and energy.
sensesIntro.cn: expenditure 意为花掉的钱、一笔经费，或时间与精力的消耗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money weighed and paid out.
core.cn: 核心意象：把钱包称量后付出去。

branches.en: The base sense is money paid out.
branches.cn: 基础义是付出的钱。

branches.en: Payments are grouped into budget lines.
branches.cn: 付款被归入预算项目。

branches.en: Paying out extends to effort and time.
branches.cn: 「付出」扩展到精力与时间。

branches.en: Total spending and single items pair together.
branches.cn: 总支出与单项经费相互对应。

branches.en: Money and energy are both resources spent.
branches.cn: 金钱与精力都是被消耗的资源。

intro.en: Expenditure builds on expend with the suffix -ure.
intro.cn: expenditure 在 expend 后加后缀 -ure。

latinIntro.en: Latin expendere and expenditura supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expendere 与 expenditura 提供核心词形。

items.example: Pendere gives the image of weighing money.
items.exampleCN: pendere 提供称量钱币的形象。

items.example: Expendere is the source of expend.
items.exampleCN: expendere 是 expend 的来源。

items.example: Expendable describes what can be lost.
items.exampleCN: expendable 描述可以消耗掉的东西。

definition_zh: 缺席；不在；缺乏；缺失
definition_en: the state of not being present, or the lack of something that ought to be there
core_image: 一把空着的椅子，桌上还留着你的杯子
scene: 教室里那把椅子空了一整个星期，老师点名时停了一下。 His long absence from class worried his classmates.
sceneCN: 这里 absence 指长时间没来上课（第 2 个义项：缺勤、缺课）；句意为他的长期缺课让同学们担心。

collocations.phrase: absence makes the heart grow fonder

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 absens 进入英语，义为「缺席的；不在的；缺乏的」
由 absent 加 -ly 构成，义为「心不在焉地」
由 absent 加 -ee 构成，义为「缺席者」，如 absentee landlord 指在外地主
由 absent 与 minded 构成的复合词，义为「心不在焉的」

senses.title: The state of not being present
senses.definition: the fact of a person or thing not being in the expected place
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物不在应有的位置这一事实
senses.example: Nobody noticed his absence until the meeting ended.
senses.exampleCN: 直到会议结束，才有人注意到他没来。
senses.why: Latin abesse is ab- 'away' plus esse 'to be', so absence is quite literally being away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abesse 是 ab-「离开」加 esse「存在」，absence 字面就是「存在到别处去了」，所以先有「不在场」。

senses.title: An occasion of missing school or work
senses.definition: a countable instance of not attending school, work or a regular duty
senses.definitionCN: 可数的一次未到校、未上班或未履行固定职责
senses.example: The teacher marked three absences in his record.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在他的记录上记了三次缺勤。
senses.why: Each time a person fails to be present, the state turns into an event that can be counted.
senses.whyCN: 每当一个人没能出现在该在的地方，那种「不在」就变成一件可数的事，于是有了「一次缺勤」。

senses.title: The lack of something that should be there
senses.definition: the state of not having something, especially a quality, fact or condition that is needed
senses.definitionCN: 指缺少某物，尤指缺少所需的性质、事实或条件
senses.example: The absence of any witnesses made the case hard to prove.
senses.exampleCN: 没有任何证人，使这个案子难以证明。
senses.why: If being can be away from a place, it can also be away from a thing: what should be there simply is not.
senses.whyCN: 如果「存在」可以离开某个地点，也可以离开某样东西：本该在那里的东西就是不在，于是义为「缺乏」。

senses.title: In the absence of: without something
senses.definition: in the phrase in the absence of, used to mean without something or because something is not available
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in the absence of，表示没有某物或因为某物不可得
senses.example: In the absence of a doctor, the nurse made the decision alone.
senses.exampleCN: 在没有医生的情况下，护士独自做了决定。
senses.why: The phrase turns the missing thing into a condition: the empty place becomes the setting for what happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把缺失的东西变成一种条件：空出来的位置成了事情发生的背景。

senses.title: Leave of absence: official time away
senses.definition: in the phrase leave of absence, formal permission to be away from work or duty for a period
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 leave of absence，指获准在一段时间内离开工作或职责
senses.example: She took a year's leave of absence to care for her father.
senses.exampleCN: 她请了一年假去照顾父亲。
senses.why: Here the absence is granted rather than regretted: the same empty place is now filled by permission.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「不在」是被批准的，而不是令人遗憾的：同一个空位，如今由许可来填补。

senses.title: Absence of mind: being distracted
senses.definition: in the phrase absence of mind, the state of not paying attention because the mind is elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 absence of mind，指心思在别处而没有留意眼前
senses.example: He signed the wrong form through a moment of absence of mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他一时心不在焉，签错了表格。
senses.why: The mind can be absent from the body just as a person is absent from a room; the same away moves inward.
senses.whyCN: 人可以从房间里「不在」，心思也可以从身体这里「不在」；同一个「离开」转向了内部，于是有了心不在焉。

senses.title: Absence makes the heart grow fonder
senses.definition: in the proverb absence makes the heart grow fonder, being apart is said to increase affection
senses.definitionCN: 用于谚语「absence makes the heart grow fonder」，指分离反而让人更添思念
senses.example: After a month apart she missed him badly; absence makes the heart grow fonder.
senses.exampleCN: 分开一个月后她非常想念他；真是离别使人情更深。
senses.why: The empty place is felt as a shape, and that shape keeps the absent person present in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 空出来的位置会被感受成一个形状，而这个形状让不在场的人一直留在心里，于是缺席反而加深了感情。

senses.title: Conspicuous by its absence
senses.definition: in the phrase conspicuous by its absence, noticeably missing from a place where it was expected
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 conspicuous by its absence，指在本该出现之处明显缺席，反而引人注意
senses.example: The star player was conspicuous by his absence from the team photo.
senses.exampleCN: 球队合影里少了那位明星球员，反而格外显眼。
senses.why: A gap in a pattern draws the eye more than a filled slot; the missing thing becomes the most visible thing.
senses.whyCN: 图案里的空缺比填满的格子更抓眼；缺失的东西反而成了最显眼的东西。

intro.en: Absence comes from the Latin verb for being, with the prefix that means away.
intro.cn: absence 来自拉丁语中表示「存在」的动词，加上表示「离开」的前缀。

items.en: Esse is the Latin verb to be; abesse, to be away, is built from ab- plus esse.
items.cn: esse 是拉丁语动词「存在、是」；abesse「不在」由 ab- 加 esse 构成。

items.en: Absens, the present participle of abesse, meant being away, and it is the source of English absent.
items.cn: absens 是 abesse 的现在分词，意为「不在的」，也是英语 absent 的来源。

items.en: Absentia is recorded in classical Latin for the state of being away, including absence from a place or from a duty.
items.cn: absentia 在古典拉丁语中已有记录，表示离开、不在的状态，包括不在某地或未尽职责。

items.en: Old French absence carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 absence 把这个名词带入英语，时在十四世纪。

items.en: English extended the word from people to things, so that a missing fact or quality could also be called an absence.
items.cn: 英语把它从人扩展到事物，缺失的事实或性质也可以称为 absence。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the absent family and one deceptive spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for lack and for not attending.
note.cn: 形近组收 absent 词族以及一个容易看错的拼写；近义组收表示缺乏与未出席的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning not present; it comes from the same Latin absens.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺席的、不在的」，与 absence 同出拉丁语 absens。

entries.definition: A person who is absent, especially from work or school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席者」，尤指缺勤者或缺课学生。

entries.definition: In a distracted way, as if the mind is somewhere else.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「心不在焉地」。

entries.definition: A bitter green liqueur; the spelling is close, but the word comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「苦艾酒」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The state of not having enough of something; it usually implies need, not mere emptiness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺乏、不足」，通常含「不够用」的意味，而不只是空着。

entries.definition: A situation in which there is not enough of something that people need.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「短缺」，指所需之物数量不足。

entries.definition: An empty space left by something missing; more literary and more physical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空缺、虚空」，更具文学与空间感。

entries.definition: The formal word for failing to be present at a required event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未出席」，是较正式的用语。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the real Latin pieces ab- and esse, and the phrases absence keeps appearing in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想使用真实的拉丁语成分 ab- 与 esse，以及 absence 实际出现的短语。

normal.en: ab- means away and esse means to be: absence is being away.
normal.cn: ab- 表示「离开」，esse 表示「存在」：absence 就是「存在在别处」。

normal.en: The same esse gives present and essence, all about being.
normal.cn: 同一个 esse 还给出 present 与 essence，都与「存在」有关。

normal.en: Absent is the adjective, absence the noun, absently the adverb.
normal.cn: absent 是形容词，absence 是名词，absently 是副词。

normal.en: Leave of absence is absence with permission attached.
normal.cn: leave of absence 是附带了许可的「不在」。

normal.en: In the absence of means the missing thing has become a condition.
normal.cn: in the absence of 表示缺失之物已经变成了一种条件。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair at a dinner table: the chair says more than any speech.
abstract.cn: 想象餐桌旁一把空椅子：这把椅子比任何话都说得更多。

abstract.en: Emptiness is never neutral; the missing thing keeps a shape in the room.
abstract.cn: 空缺从不中性；缺失之物会在房间里留下一个形状。

abstract.en: The mind can be absent from the body, which is why the word also names distraction.
abstract.cn: 心思可以从身体里缺席，所以这个词也用来指心不在焉。

examples.en: Nobody noticed his absence until the meeting ended.
examples.cn: 直到会议结束，才有人注意到他没来。

examples.en: In the absence of proof, the court had to dismiss the charge.
examples.cn: 由于缺乏证据，法庭不得不撤销指控。

examples.en: Her absence from school was explained by a bad cold.
examples.cn: 她缺课的原因是一场重感冒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布森斯」——桌上的杯子还在，人却不在：缺席、缺乏。

root: 拉丁语 absentia，来自 absens（不在的），后者是 abesse（不在）的现在分词：ab-「离开」+ esse「存在」。古法语 absence 于十四世纪把该词带入英语。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses start from one empty place: a person missing, an event counted, a thing lacking, a phrase built on that lack, or a gap that becomes meaningful.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个空位出发：缺了一个人、数出一次缺席、少了一样东西、由缺失构成的短语，或一个有意义的空缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair with a cup still standing on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把空椅子，桌上的杯子还在。

branches.en: THE PERSON: not being there, and each countable failure to attend.
branches.cn: 人物线：不在这里，以及每一次可以计数的未到场。

branches.en: THE THING: a missing fact or quality, and the condition built from that lack.
branches.cn: 事物线：缺失的事实或性质，以及由这种缺乏构成的条件。

branches.en: THE PERMISSION: leave of absence is the empty place officially approved.
branches.cn: 许可线：leave of absence 是被正式批准的空位。

branches.en: THE MIND: absence of mind turns the gap inward.
branches.cn: 心智线：absence of mind 把这种空缺转向内部。

branches.en: THE PARADOX: the gap deepens feeling, or becomes the most visible thing in the frame.
branches.cn: 悖论线：空缺加深了感情，或者成了画面里最显眼的东西。

intro.en: Absence is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb of being and a noun ending, all of which reappear across English.
intro.cn: absence 由一个拉丁前缀、一个表示「存在」的拉丁动词和一个名词词尾构成，这三部分在英语里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are all recorded, so nothing here needs reconstruction except the deeper Indo-European layer.
latinIntro.cn: 下面这些拉丁语形式都有文献记录，除更早的印欧语层次外无需重构。

items.example: It marks movement away from a point.
items.exampleCN: 它标示从事物离开的运动。

items.example: Esse is the root of essence.
items.exampleCN: esse 是 essence 的词根。

items.example: The verb names being somewhere else.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词表示「在别处存在」。

items.example: The noun names the empty place.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名那个空位。

items.meaning: the state of not being present
items.example: The word entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个词经由法语进入英语。

items.example: It forms nouns such as presence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 presence 一类的名词。

items.exampleCN: 她心不在焉地点了点头。

items.exampleCN: 每到冬天，缺勤名单都会变长。

definition_zh: 各种各样的；不同的、好几个的；多方面的
definition_en: of several different kinds or several different people or things
core_image: 一排货架上摆着颜色形状各不相同的盒子，标签却写着同一类商品
scene: 聚会结束后，桌上留下了各色各样的杯子，高矮粗细都不相同。 Various guests arrived through the evening, each with a different story.
sceneCN: 这里 various 是「各种各样的」（第 1 个义项：种类不止一种）；句意为整晚陆续来了各种各样的客人，每人都有不同的故事。一排彼此不同的盒子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：各种各样的；不同的、好几个的；多方面的

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「以各种方式、不同地」
名词，义为「多样性、种类」，是本词的名词形式
动词，义为「变化、不同」
名词，义为「多样性」，较少使用
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」

senses.title: Of several kinds
senses.titleCN: 各种各样的：种类不止一个
senses.definition: of more than one kind, used before a plural noun
senses.definitionCN: 不止一种，用在复数名词前
senses.example: Various guests arrived through the evening, each with a different story.
senses.exampleCN: 整晚陆续来了各种各样的客人，每人都有不同的故事。
senses.why: Latin varius means spotted or mixed; various names a set whose members do not match.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的；various 指成员彼此不一致的一组。

senses.title: Several and different
senses.titleCN: 好几个不同的：数量不定但都算在内
senses.definition: several different people or things, not exactly numbered
senses.definitionCN: 几个不同的人或物，数量不确切
senses.example: We met at various times during the year.
senses.exampleCN: 我们这一年里在不同时间见过几次。
senses.why: The word avoids giving a number; it counts only as far as several and no further.
senses.whyCN: 这个词回避给出具体数目：只数到「好几个」为止。

senses.title: From many sides
senses.titleCN: 多方面的：原因、来源各不相同
senses.definition: coming from many different sources or aspects
senses.definitionCN: 来自许多不同来源或方面
senses.example: The delay was due to various reasons, some of them personal.
senses.exampleCN: 延误有种种原因，其中一些是私人的。
senses.why: Each member of the set has its own origin; the word holds them side by side.
senses.whyCN: 这一组的每个成员各有来源，这个词把它们并排放着。

senses.title: Many-sided in skill
senses.titleCN: 多样化的：本事不止一样（较少用）
senses.definition: having many different abilities or forms, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 具有多种才能或形态，较旧的文学用法
senses.example: He is a various man, at home in both music and mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个多才之人，音乐和数学都能应付。
senses.why: The older sense applies the diversity to a single person, not to a group.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的含义把多样性用在一个人身上，而不是一群人身上。

intro.en: Various is the English form of Latin varius, spotted or mixed, with an adjective ending added on the way.
intro.cn: various 是拉丁语 varius「斑驳的、混杂的」在英语里的形态，途中加上了形容词词尾。

items.en: The adjective varius described things of mixed colour, uneven or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述颜色混杂、不齐整或多种多样的事物。

items.en: Its plural varii was used for several different people, close to the modern sense.
items.cn: 其复数 varii 用于指若干不同的人，很接近现代含义。

items.en: English formed various from the Latin stem, first meaning changeable or diverse.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词干造出 various，最初意为易变的或多样的。

items.en: Modern usage settles it before plural nouns, meaning several different.
items.cn: 现代用法把它固定在复数名词前，表示好几个不同的。

items.en: The word now shares its family with variety, variable and vary, all from the same Latin stem.
items.cn: 它如今与 variety、variable、vary 共用一个家族，全部出自同一拉丁词干。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds quantifiers for a loose plurality.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示不确切多数的限定词。

entries.definition: The noun for many kinds or one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」。

entries.definition: The verb, to differ or change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」。

entries.definition: Made varied, not all alike; close to various in sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，意义接近 various。

entries.definition: Able to change, or a symbol that varies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: More than two but not many, without the sense of unlike.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「几个」，不强调彼此不同。

entries.definition: Not the same as one another, the core of various.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不同的」，是 various 的核心义。

entries.definition: Of mixed kinds put together, often in a box or pack.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「什锦的、搭配好的」。

entries.definition: Many in number, with no emphasis on variety.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「众多的」，不强调种类。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the prefix habit of various and real collocations such as for various reasons.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用 various 只修饰复数的习惯，以及 for various reasons 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Various always sits before a plural noun: various reasons, never various reason.
normal.cn: various 总在复数名词前：various reasons，不能接单数。

normal.en: Various means more than one, but it refuses to say how many.
normal.cn: various 表示不止一个，却不肯说有几个。

normal.en: For various reasons is a polite way to avoid listing the reasons.
normal.cn: for various reasons 是避免一一列举的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Varied describes a thing, various describes a group of things.
normal.cn: varied 形容一样东西，various 形容一组东西。

normal.en: The same root gives variety, vary and variable.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还给出 variety、vary 与 variable。

abstract.en: Various is a quiet way of saying that a group refuses to be summed up in one word.
abstract.cn: various 是一个低调的说法：这一组无法用一个词概括。

abstract.en: The word is plural by nature; it draws its meaning from the gaps between members.
abstract.cn: 这个词天生带复数性：它的意思来自成员之间的差异。

abstract.en: Say various and you admit you have not checked everything, only that the pieces differ.
abstract.cn: 说 various 就等于承认你并未逐一核对，只确认了它们互不相同。

examples.en: Various people offered to help with the move.
examples.cn: 有好几个人主动提出帮忙搬家。

examples.en: The delay was caused by various problems with the engine.
examples.cn: 延误差是由发动机的种种问题造成的。

examples.en: Books on the subject are available in various languages.
examples.cn: 这个主题的书有各种语言的版本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我瑞爱死」——各式各样的东西我瑞（锐）意爱死：各种各样的

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 varius「斑驳的、多种的」，经英语自造词 various 进入使用；同族词有 variety、vary、variation、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Various ranges from many kinds before a plural noun, to an unnumbered several, many sources, and an older sense of many-sided.
sensesIntro.cn: various 从复数名词前的「多种」，到不确切的好几个、多来源，以及较旧的「多才」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf of boxes, same category, every shape and colour different.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排货架上的盒子同属一类，却个个形状颜色不同。

branches.en: KIND LINE: the members are not alike.
branches.cn: 种类线：成员彼此并不相同。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: several, with no exact number.
branches.cn: 计数线：好几个，不给具体数字。

branches.en: ORIGIN LINE: causes and sources differ.
branches.cn: 来源线：原因与出处各异。

branches.en: ABILITY LINE: one person with many sides.
branches.cn: 才能线：一个人有多面。

branches.en: CONTRAST: various refuses both one word and a fixed number.
branches.cn: 对照线：various 既不肯概括，也不肯给数。

intro.en: Various is a Latin stem with an English adjective ending; the whole vari- family shares the stem.
intro.cn: various 是拉丁词干加英语形容词词尾，整个 vari- 家族共用该词干。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is varius; the plural varii already meant several different people.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 varius，其复数 varii 已经表示「若干不同的人」。

definition_zh: 可能性；可能的事；潜力
definition_en: the chance that something may happen, a possible event, or the capacity for future development
core_image: 一扇没上锁的门，门后还看不清
scene: 面试结束后，主管没有当场答复，只说还要再议一次。 There is a real possibility that the job will go to another candidate.
sceneCN: 这里 possibility 是「可能性」（第 1 个义项：某事可能发生）；句意为这份工作很可能落到另一位候选人手里。画面里有面试桌和未落笔的记录纸。

derivatives.zh: 源自拉丁 possibilis，义为「可能的」
possible 加 -ly，义为「也许；可能」
im-（不）加 possible，义为「不可能的」

senses.title: The chance that something may happen
senses.definition: the fact that something may happen or may be true, without certainty
senses.definitionCN: 某事可能发生或可能为真，但并不确定
senses.example: There is a real possibility that the flight will be delayed.
senses.exampleCN: 航班延误的可能性确实存在。
senses.why: The word starts from Latin posse, to be able: what is possible is what can come to be, so the core sense is an open future rather than a fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始于拉丁语 posse（能够）：可能的就是能够出现的，所以核心义是一个尚未关闭的未来，而不是既成事实。

senses.title: A possible event or result
senses.definition: a single thing that may happen, or one of several results you can imagine
senses.definitionCN: 某一件可能发生的事，或你能设想到的若干结果之一
senses.example: We must prepare for several possibilities before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会前我们必须为几种可能的情况做准备。
senses.why: If possibility is the open future in general, counting those openings turns the abstract quality into separate items on a list.
senses.whyCN: 如果 possibility 泛指未定的未来，那么把这些开口一个个数出来，抽象性质就变成清单上分开的条目。

senses.title: The chance to develop or succeed
senses.definition: the opportunities a person, place or plan has for future growth, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 人、地方或计划在未来成长上的机会，常用复数
senses.example: The young player still has great possibilities.
senses.exampleCN: 这名年轻球员仍有很大的发展潜力。
senses.why: An unwritten future can belong to a person as well as to an event, and then the word points to unused capacity rather than to sheer chance.
senses.whyCN: 未被写定的未来既属于事件，也属于人；这时词义指向尚未用上的能力，而不是纯粹的偶然。

intro.en: Possibility comes from Latin posse, to be able, and it reached English through the adjective possibilis and the noun possibilitas before French passed it on.
intro.cn: possibility 来自拉丁语 posse（能够），先有形容词 possibilis 与名词 possibilitas，再由法语传给英语。

items.en: Latin posse, to be able, is generally analysed as potis, able, plus esse, to be, so ability was phrased as being in a position to be.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 posse（能够）由 potis（有能力的）加 esse（是、存在）构成，能力被说成「处于能够存在的状态」。

items.en: The adjective possibilis described something that can be or can happen, adding -bilis, the suffix of capability.
items.cn: 形容词 possibilis 描述能够存在或能够发生的事物，加的是表示「能够被……」的后缀 -bilis。

items.en: Late Latin coined possibilitas for the quality of being possible, a noun built on the adjective rather than on the verb.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语造出 possibilitas 表示「可能」这一性质，这个名词建立在形容词而非动词之上。

items.en: Old French possibilité passed the word to English, where it first named the abstract quality before it named concrete chances.
items.cn: 古法语的 possibilité 把词传给英语，它先指抽象的性质，之后才指具体的机会。

items.en: Modern English uses possibility for a chance, for a single possible event, and for the untapped powers a person or a plan may hold.
items.cn: 现代英语用 possibility 指机会、指单件可能发生的事，也指人或计划尚未发挥的潜力。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same Latin adjective of capability; the near-meaning group gathers words for chance and for what may come.
note.cn: 形近组建立在同一个表示「能够」的拉丁形容词上；近义组收表示机会与未来之事的词。

entries.definition: The adjective that says something can be or can happen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，表示某事能够存在或发生。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning perhaps or in a way that can be done.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，表示也许，或以可行的方式。

entries.definition: Not able to be or to happen, formed with the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀构成，表示不可能存在或发生。

entries.definition: The negative noun that mirrors this word exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 与这个词完全对应的否定名词。

entries.definition: How likely it is that something will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能程度。

entries.definition: The measured probability that something will occur.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事发生概率的衡量。

entries.definition: Something that may happen in the future, often hoped for.
entries.definitionCN: 未来可能发生的事，常指所期望的。

entries.definition: The ability or quality that exists but is not yet used.
entries.definitionCN: 已存在但尚未发挥的能力或特质。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from the Latin verb for being able, and its family keeps returning to capability, chance and what has not yet happened.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「能够」的拉丁动词构成，词族反复回到能力、机会以及尚未发生的事。

normal.en: Posse, to be able, is analysed as potis plus esse, able plus to be, so possibility is literally a way of being that can still arrive.
normal.cn: posse（能够）可分析为 potis 加 esse，即「有能力」加「存在」，所以 possibility 字面上是一种还可能到来的存在方式。

normal.en: The suffix -bilis marks what can be done or can exist, and it is the same ending hidden in visible and flexible.
normal.cn: 后缀 -bilis 标出「能够被做成或能够存在」的东西，visible 与 flexible 里藏的也是这个结尾。

normal.en: The ending -ity turns the adjective possible into the noun possibility, naming the quality itself.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ity 把形容词 possible 变成名词 possibility，命名的是这种性质本身。

normal.en: The plural possibilities often means chances to develop, as in the possibilities of a young player.
normal.cn: 复数 possibilities 常指发展的机会，例如一名年轻球员的可能性。

normal.en: Impossible adds im-, not, to possible, and impossibility mirrors possibility with the same negative prefix.
normal.cn: impossible 在 possible 前加表示否定的 im-，impossibility 也用同一个否定前缀与 possibility 对应。

abstract.en: An unlocked door with the room still dark: that is possibility before it hardens into an event.
abstract.cn: 一扇没锁的门，屋里还黑着：这就是尚未变成事件之前的可能性。

abstract.en: A list of possible results is simply the open future cut into countable pieces.
abstract.cn: 一张可能结果的清单，不过是被切成可数碎片的开放未来。

abstract.en: To say a person is full of possibilities is to say the future has not spent itself on them yet.
abstract.cn: 说一个人充满可能性，意思是未来还没有在他身上用完。

examples.en: There is a real possibility that the flight will be delayed.
examples.cn: 航班延误的可能性确实存在。

examples.en: We must prepare for several possibilities before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前我们必须为几种可能的情况做准备。

examples.en: The young player still has great possibilities.
examples.cn: 这名年轻球员仍有很大的发展潜力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕是必能」——凡事都想着「怕是也能」，就是给自己留了一种可能；possibility 是可能性。

root: 拉丁语 posse（能够）通常分析为 potis（有能力的）加 esse（是、存在），再由 possibilis（可能的）与晚期拉丁 possibilitas 发展而来；它与 possess 一族共享 potis，但走的是「能够」这一条线。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an outcome that can still happen; the senses then count single possible events and, finally, point at powers not yet used.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个仍可能发生的结果；义项由此数出单件可能之事，最后指向尚未用上的能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unlocked door with the room beyond still in darkness.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇没有上锁的门，门后的房间还在暗处。

branches.en: a letter that may or may not arrive
branches.cn: 可能来也可能不来的信

branches.en: three routes drawn on a napkin
branches.cn: 餐巾纸上画出的三条路线

branches.en: a young voice still finding its range
branches.cn: 还在找音域的年轻嗓音

branches.en: a delay announced but not yet dated
branches.cn: 宣布了却还没定日期的延误

branches.en: two futures folded into one name
branches.cn: 折在同一个名字里的两种未来

intro.en: A Latin verb of being able, its adjective of capability, and the noun endings that name a quality hold the word together.
intro.cn: 一个表示「能够」的拉丁动词、它的能力形容词，以及命名性质的名词词尾，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are recorded: posse, possibilis and possibilitas, with potis as the element shared with the possess family.
latinIntro.cn: 这些拉丁词形都有记录：posse、possibilis 与 possibilitas，其中 potis 是与 possess 一族共有的成分。

definition_zh: 发言人；代言人
definition_en: a person chosen to speak officially for a group, organization, or another person
core_image: 一排话筒前的人：身后组织的所有话，都从他嘴里出来
scene: 新闻发布厅里闪光灯亮成一片。 The company spokesman read a short statement to the reporters.
sceneCN: 这里 spokesman 是「发言人」（第 1 个义项：代表组织正式发言者）；句意为公司发言人向记者宣读了一份简短声明。图中可辨识物件：话筒、发布会讲台、闪光灯。

derivatives.zh: 同词构词的阴性形式，义为「女发言人」
中性化形式，义为「发言人（不区分性别）」
本词复数形式
构词基础动词，义为「说话」

senses.title: One who speaks for a group
senses.definition: a person selected to make statements on behalf of others
senses.definitionCN: 被选定代表他人发声的人
senses.example: A union spokesman answered the pay questions.
senses.exampleCN: 工会发言人回答了薪酬问题。
senses.why: One mouth is placed before many: the crowd's words travel through a single throat.
senses.whyCN: 一张嘴被放在众人之前：人群的话经由一副喉咙说出。

senses.title: An official media contact
senses.definition: the designated contact who gives statements to journalists
senses.definitionCN: 被指定向记者发布声明的人
senses.example: The ministry spokesman confirmed the date of the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 部委发言人确认了会谈日期。
senses.why: The office builds a wall of process, and the spokesman is its speaking gate.
senses.whyCN: 机关筑起程序的墙，发言人是墙上那道会说话的门。

senses.title: Spokesman or spokesperson usage
senses.titleCN: spokesman 与 spokesperson 的用法
senses.definition: spokesman is traditional; spokesperson avoids marking gender
senses.definitionCN: spokesman 是传统形式；spokesperson 不标性别
senses.example: The press office now prefers the term spokesperson.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻办公室现在更倾向用 spokesperson 一词。
senses.why: Language remodels the old compound to fit the modern crowd.
senses.whyCN: 语言改造旧复合词以适应现代人群。

senses.title: In history: one who speaks up for a cause
senses.definition: a person who speaks up for a cause or movement
senses.definitionCN: 为某事业或运动公开发声的人
senses.example: The movement found its spokesman in a young lawyer.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动在一位年轻律师身上找到了代言人。
senses.why: A cause without a voice stays invisible; one speaker makes it seen.
senses.whyCN: 无声的事业无影无形；一个发声者让它显形。

senses.title: The genitive line: spokes of speech
senses.titleCN: 构词里的属格：说话之口
senses.definition: the word contains an old genitive: one man of speaking
senses.definitionCN: 该词含有古老的属格：属于「说话」的那个人
senses.example: The -s in spokesman is an old possessive, like in statesman.
senses.exampleCN: spokesman 中的 -s 是古老的属格标记，如 statesman 中的用法。
senses.why: Old English grammar hides inside the compound like a fossil in stone.
senses.whyCN: 古英语语法像石中化石一样藏在复合词里。

senses.title: Spokes as radiating lines
senses.definition: the nouns spoke (wheel bar) and spokesman share nothing historically, yet the wheel image helps memory
senses.definitionCN: spoke（轮辐）与 spokesman 词源无关，但轮辐意象有助记忆
senses.example: Like the spokes of a wheel, every statement runs from the centre through him.
senses.exampleCN: 如轮辐一般，每条声明都从中心经由他发出。
senses.why: The image is a memory aid only, not a real relative.
senses.whyCN: 这只是记忆辅助，并非真正的亲族。

senses.title: A spokesman against something
senses.definition: one who officially voices opposition for others
senses.definitionCN: 代表众人正式表达反对的人
senses.example: She acted as spokesman for the objecting residents.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任反对居民们的代言人。
senses.why: The gate swings both ways: it can carry refusal as well as approval.
senses.whyCN: 这扇门双向开合：既承载赞成，也承载拒绝。

senses.title: Figurative: the face of a thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that symbolically represents an organization
senses.definitionCN: 象征性地代表某组织的人或物
senses.example: The veteran captain became the team's public spokesman.
senses.exampleCN: 老队长成了球队的公众门面。
senses.why: When a face is needed, the crowd picks the steadiest one.
senses.whyCN: 需要一张脸时，人群会挑最稳的那一张。

intro.en: Spokesman is an English compound with an old grammar fossil inside it.
intro.cn: spokesman 是英语复合词，内部藏着一枚古语法的化石。

items.en: Old English genitive speca meant "of speech", a possessive form of spec "speech".
items.cn: 古英语属格 speca 意为「言语的」，是 spec「言语」的所有格形式。

items.en: Compounds like spokesman and statesman keep this old genitive -s.
items.cn: spokesman、statesman 等复合词保留了这一古老的属格 -s。

items.en: Middle English spoke(s)man meant "one who speaks for another".
items.cn: 中古英语 spoke(s)man 意为「代他人发言者」。

items.en: The modern word settled in the seventeenth century for official representatives.
items.cn: 现代形式于十七世纪定型，指官方代表。

items.en: Spokeswoman and spokesperson arose in the twentieth century for inclusive usage.
items.cn: spokeswoman 与 spokesperson 产生于二十世纪，以实现无性别指向的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the speaking family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for representation.
note.cn: 形近组收「说话」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示代表身份的词。

entries.definition: One who acts or votes for others, broader than speaking only.
entries.definitionCN: 代他人行事或投票者，范围比仅发言更广。

entries.definition: One sent to act for others, often at meetings.
entries.definitionCN: 被派遣代表他人者，多指会议场合。

entries.definition: An informal, often critical word for one who relays another's views.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式且常含贬义，指传声筒。

entries.definition: An official messenger sent between governments.
entries.definitionCN: 政府间派出的正式使者。

entries.definition: One who pleads a cause publicly for others.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人公开申辩、鼓吹者。

normal.cn: spokes + man：-s 是古老属格，即「属于说话的人」。

normal.en: Statesman hides the same fossil: the man of the state.
normal.cn: statesman 藏着同一化石：「属于国家的人」。

normal.en: A spokesman for the company speaks with the company's voice.

normal.en: The neutral word spokesperson avoids marking gender.

normal.en: Picture every wheel spoke running from the hub through one rim point.
normal.cn: 想象每根轮辐都从轴心通向轮缘同一点。

abstract.en: One mouth at the microphone, a hundred silent mouths behind it.
abstract.cn: 话筒前一张嘴，身后一百张沉默的嘴。

abstract.en: The hub speaks only through the spokes it has chosen.
abstract.cn: 轴心只通过它选定的轮辐说话。

abstract.en: When the compound grows a W or a PERSON, the gate widens for all.
abstract.cn: 复合词长出 W 或 PERSON，那扇门就向所有人敞开。

examples.en: A police spokesman said the investigation was continuing.
examples.cn: 警方发言人表示调查仍在进行。

examples.en: The union spokesman rejected the pay offer on live television.
examples.cn: 工会发言人在电视直播中拒绝了薪酬方案。

examples.cn: 她担任反对建筑方案的居民代言人。

definition_zh: 肯定地；明确地；当然
definition_en: without any doubt, or in a clear and firm way
core_image: 一句回答落地，没有留下商量的余地
scene: 朋友在门口问周末到底来不来，她一边系鞋带一边点头。 I will definitely be there on Saturday.
sceneCN: 这里 definitely 指「肯定地」（第 1 个义项：毫无怀疑）；句意是星期六我一定会到。

derivatives.zh: 明确的；确定的
定义
定义；界定
明确；确定性

senses.title: Without any doubt
senses.definition: used to say that something is certainly true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明某事确实为真或一定发生
senses.example: I will definitely be there on Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 星期六我一定会到。
senses.why: A promise with no space left in it is easier to keep.
senses.whyCN: 没留空隙的承诺，反而更容易守住。

senses.title: In a clear and firm way
senses.definition: in a manner that leaves no room for another reading
senses.definitionCN: 所说的话不容许别的理解
senses.example: She spoke definitely about the closing date.
senses.exampleCN: 她把截止日期说得很明确。
senses.why: Firm speech is a line that does not bend when pressed.
senses.whyCN: 坚定的说法，是一条压也不弯的线。

senses.title: As a warm yes in talk
senses.definition: used in speech to agree strongly with a suggestion
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于强烈赞同某个提议
senses.example: Definitely, let us take the early train.
senses.exampleCN: 当然，我们就坐早班车。
senses.why: Agreement, said with force, becomes a small gift.
senses.whyCN: 用力说出的赞同，就是一份小小的礼物。

intro.en: Definitely is definite plus -ly; its parents are Latin finis, a boundary, and the prefix de-.
intro.cn: definitely 是 definite 加 -ly，父母是拉丁语的 finis（边界）与前缀 de-。

items.en: Definitus meant bounded and settled.
items.cn: definitus 意为有界的、已定的。

items.en: Definit reached French with the sense of certain.
items.cn: definit 带着「确实」的意思进入法语。

items.en: Definite settled into English as an adjective.
items.cn: definite 作为形容词在英语里安定下来。

items.en: The adverb definitely appeared in letters and records.
items.cn: 副词 definitely 出现在书信与文书里。

items.en: In speech it has become a friendly, emphatic yes.
items.cn: 在口语里它已经变成一个热情而强调的「是」。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by small endings, and the meaning group is made of three ways to say for sure.
note.cn: 形近组只差很小的词尾，近义组则由三种「说准了」的方式组成。

entries.definition: clear and not open to doubt
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而不容怀疑的

entries.definition: final and authoritative
entries.definitionCN: 最终的、具权威的

entries.definition: openly refusing to obey
entries.definitionCN: 公然不肯服从的

entries.definition: without any doubt at all
entries.definitionCN: 毫无怀疑地

entries.definition: used when one expects agreement
entries.definitionCN: 用于期待对方同意时

entries.definition: completely and without limit
entries.definitionCN: 完全地、毫无保留地

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a nod at the door and end with an agreement that sounds like a gift.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门口的一个点头开始，落到听起来像礼物的赞同。

normal.en: A yes said slowly is worth more than a maybe said often.
normal.cn: 慢慢说出的「是」，比常常说的「也许」更值钱。

normal.en: A date given definitely can be written in ink.
normal.cn: 说得肯定的日期，才可以拿钢笔写。

normal.en: When the answer is clear, the voice drops instead of rising.
normal.cn: 答案清楚时，声音是往下落，不是往上扬。

normal.en: Definitely carries a line at its middle; that line is the fence.
normal.cn: definitely 中间带着一条线，那条线就是篱笆。

normal.en: Add -ly to definite and certainty becomes a way of speaking.
normal.cn: definite 加 -ly，确定就成了一种说话方式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand laid flat on a table to end a discussion.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平放在桌上，把讨论按住。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence written in ink with no eraser nearby.
abstract.cn: 想象一句用墨水写下的话，旁边没有橡皮。

abstract.en: Picture a nod given before the question is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象问题还没说完，头已经点下去了。

examples.cn: 星期六我一定会到。

examples.en: She spoke definitely about the closing date.
examples.cn: 她把截止日期说得很明确。

examples.en: Definitely, let us take the early train.
examples.cn: 当然，我们就坐早班车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 definitely 记成「定分你特利」：定得分明，说话才干脆，就是肯定地。

root: 由 definite 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，而 definite 来自拉丁语 definitus（有界的、已定的），词根 finis 是边界。界线一画定，说话就不留余地，因此这个词既表示毫无疑问，也表示语气明确，口语里还成了热情的「当然」。

sensesIntro.en: From a promise with no gap, to a firm sentence, to a warm yes at the door.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有缝隙的承诺，到一句坚定的说明，再到门口那声热情的「当然」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an answer that lands flat and stays.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句回答落地，就停在那里不动。

branches.en: The first sense is certainty about what will happen.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是对将要发生之事的确定。

branches.en: The same certainty, in the mouth, becomes firm speech.
branches.cn: 同样的确定进了嘴里，就是坚定的说法。

branches.en: Said to a friend, the firm word turns into warmth.
branches.cn: 对朋友说出时，坚定的词就变成了暖意。

branches.en: Both senses refuse to leave a door open for doubt.
branches.cn: 两个义项都不肯给怀疑留一扇门。

branches.en: A firm answer and a warm yes are the same word at different heat.
branches.cn: 坚定的答复与热情的赞同，是同一个词的不同温度。

intro.en: Definitely is built from definite and -ly, and the family around it is all about limits.
intro.cn: definitely 由 definite 与 -ly 构成，周围那一族词全都与界限有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with the prefix de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.exampleCN: 我们定了一个明确的计划。

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；表面上的；貌似的
definition_en: easy to see or understand; also seeming rather than certainly true
core_image: 东西浮到表面，一眼就看见，却未必是全部
scene: 清晨的湖面起了薄雾，岸边的船影慢慢清晰起来。 It became apparent that the ferry would not sail that day.
sceneCN: 这里 apparent 是「明显的」（第 1 个义项：事情变得清楚，一眼就能看出来）；句意为「情况变得很明显，那天渡轮不会开航」。画面里有清晨的湖面、薄雾和渐渐清晰的船影。

pos.zh: 形容词：明显的；显而易见的；表面上的；貌似的

collocations.zh: 法定继承人；公认的接班者

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「显然；据说」
与本词同出拉丁语 apparere，义为「出现；显得」
由同一拉丁词根 apparere 派生，义为「幽灵；幻影」

senses.title: Easy to see or understand
senses.definition: clearly visible or easily understood, so that no doubt remains
senses.definitionCN: 清楚可见或容易理解，以至于不再有疑问
senses.example: It became apparent that the ferry would not sail that day.
senses.exampleCN: 情况变得很明显，那天渡轮不会开航。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'come into sight'; what has come into sight is no longer hidden, which is precisely the sense of 'obvious'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是「进入视野」；进入视野的东西不再被遮住，这正是「显而易见」的意思。

senses.title: Seeming rather than certain
senses.definition: appearing to be true on the surface, though it may not be so in reality
senses.definitionCN: 表面上看来如此，实际上未必如此
senses.example: The apparent calm of the town hid a great deal of worry.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇表面上的平静掩盖了许多忧虑。
senses.why: The same word that reports what is seen can also warn that only the surface has been seen, so 'apparent' comes to mark a possible illusion.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既能报告所见，也能提醒所见只是表面，于是 apparent 转而标记一种可能的假象。

senses.title: Visible to the eye
senses.definition: able to be seen, especially in astronomy for a star or planet visible without aid
senses.definitionCN: 能够被看见，尤用于天文学，指无需仪器即可看见的恒星或行星
senses.example: The comet is apparent to the naked eye only before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗彗星只有在天亮前才能用肉眼看见。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical layer: before the word meant 'obvious' it simply meant 'showing itself to sight'.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体层：在表示「明显」之前，它只是「把自己显给视觉看」的意思。

senses.title: Undisputed, as in heir apparent
senses.titleCN: 确定的；无可争议的（用于 heir apparent）
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase heir apparent, clearly next in line and not to be displaced by a later claimant
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定短语 heir apparent，指明确排在下一位、不会被后来者取代的继承者
senses.example: She was the heir apparent to the old bookstore.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那家旧书店公认的接班人。
senses.why: If a right is apparent to everyone, it is beyond dispute; the legal phrase borrows that clarity for succession.
senses.whyCN: 如果一项权利对所有人都显而易见，它就无可争议；这个法律短语把这份清楚借给了继承次序。

intro.en: Apparent comes from a Latin verb meaning 'come into sight', so its oldest sense is visual rather than logical.
intro.cn: apparent 来自一个表示「进入视野」的拉丁动词，因此它最古老的义项是视觉的，而不是逻辑的。

items.en: Apparere meant 'come into view, show oneself', built from ad- 'to' and parere 'come forth, be visible'.
items.cn: apparere 表示「进入视野、显现自身」，由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现、可见」构成。

items.en: The present participle aparant 'being visible' passes into English as an adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 aparant「可见的、显现的」作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: English apparent first means 'visible, manifest', used of things that can be seen with the eyes.
items.cn: 英语 apparent 最初义为「可见的、显现的」，用于可以用眼睛看见的事物。

items.en: The sense widens from sight to understanding: what is plainly seen becomes what is plainly understood.
items.cn: 词义从视觉扩展到理解：看得清楚的东西变成理解得清楚的东西。

items.en: The qualifying sense 'seeming, not necessarily real' develops, often in contrast with 'actual'.
items.cn: 限定性的「表面上、未必真实」义发展出来，常与 actual 形成对照。

items.en: Both senses coexist: apparent facts are clear, while apparent calm may be only on the surface.
items.cn: 两种义项并存：apparent facts 是清楚的事实，而 apparent calm 可能只停留在表面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family from the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for clarity and for mere appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收同出那个拉丁动词的一族词；近义组收表示清楚与仅止于表面的词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning seemingly, or as far as one can tell.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「看来；据说」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to come into sight or to seem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现；显得」，与本词同出拉丁语 apparere。

entries.definition: A noun meaning the act of appearing or the look of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出现；外表」，同出 apparere 这一词根。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a ghostly figure that suddenly appears.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幽灵、幻影」，指突然显现的身影。

entries.definition: So clear that it needs no explanation or effort to see.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚到不需要解释或费力去看，语气比 apparent 更直接。

entries.definition: Clear from the evidence, often in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 由证据而显得清楚，常见于正式文字，语气比 apparent 更书面。

entries.definition: Appearing to be true without being proved so.
entries.definitionCN: 看来如此却未被证实，与 apparent 的「表面上」义最接近。

entries.definition: Stated or shown outwardly, often with a hint of doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 对外宣称或显示的，常暗含怀疑，比 apparent 更强调「名义上的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'come into sight' verb and the two opposite directions the adjective took.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「进入视野」动词，以及这个形容词走出的两个相反方向。

normal.en: The core verb means 'come into sight': what appears is what can be seen.
normal.cn: 核心动词意为「进入视野」：显现出来的，就是能看见的。

normal.en: From sight it moves to understanding: apparent facts are plain facts.
normal.cn: 从视觉转到理解：apparent facts 就是明摆着的事实。

normal.en: Then it learns to hedge: apparent calm may be only on the surface.
normal.cn: 然后它学会留余地：apparent calm 可能只停留在表面。

normal.en: The fixed frame is it became apparent that, followed by a clause.
normal.cn: 固定句式是 it became apparent that，后面接一个从句。

normal.en: The legal phrase heir apparent keeps the 'undisputed' edge.
normal.cn: 法律短语 heir apparent 保留了「无可争议」的锋利。

abstract.en: Picture an object rising to the surface of dark water and catching the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一件东西从深水里浮到水面，被光一照。

abstract.en: The word is a surface, not a depth: it shows what can be seen, not what is hidden below.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一个表面而不是深处：它展示看得见的，而不是藏在下头的。

abstract.en: Hence the double edge: what is apparent may be the whole truth or only its skin.
abstract.cn: 由此生出双刃：apparent 的东西可能是全部真相，也可能只是它的表皮。

examples.en: It soon became apparent that no one had brought the key.
examples.cn: 很快就明显看出，没有人带钥匙。

examples.en: The apparent calm of the town hid a great deal of worry.
examples.cn: 小镇表面上的平静掩盖了许多忧虑。

examples.en: For no apparent reason, the lights went out.
examples.cn: 没有任何明显理由，灯就灭了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额怕认特」——雾散船影显现，他说「怕认错，先看清」：明显的

root: apparent 经古法语 aparant 来自拉丁语 apparere「进入视野、显现」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现、可见」构成。十四世纪英语义为「可见的、显现的」；十六世纪由视觉扩展到理解，义为「明显的」；十七世纪发展出「表面上、未必真实」的限定义，常与 actual 对照；现代两种义项并存，并有固定短语 heir apparent。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses fan out from 'come into sight': the plainly visible fact, the surface that may deceive, the astronomical object seen by eye, and the undisputed successor.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法从「进入视野」展开：明摆着的事实、可能骗人的表面、肉眼可见的天体，以及无可争议的接班人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something rising to the surface and catching the light, while the depth stays unseen.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物浮到表面被光照见，而深处仍看不见。

branches.en: THE CLARITY LINE: what has appeared is no longer in doubt.
branches.cn: 清楚线：已经显现的东西不再令人怀疑。

branches.en: THE SURFACE LINE: only the skin has been seen, so truth is still open.
branches.cn: 表面线：只看见了表皮，真相仍悬着。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: the oldest sense, visible without aid.
branches.cn: 肉眼线：最古老的义项，无需仪器即可看见。

branches.en: THE SUCCESSION LINE: a right clear to all cannot be disputed.
branches.cn: 继承线：对所有人都清楚的权利，无法被争辩。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE EDGE LINE: the same word certifies and cautions.
branches.cn: 双刃线：同一个词既作担保，也作提醒。

intro.en: Apparent is a Latin borrowing, and its parts are the prefix ad- and the verb parere 'come forth'.
intro.cn: apparent 是拉丁语借词，它的构件是前缀 ad- 与动词 parere「出现」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is direct: apparere is the verb behind apparent, appear and apparition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语血统是直接的：apparere 正是 apparent、appear 与 apparition 背后的动词。

items.example: The reason for the delay was apparent to all.
items.exampleCN: 延误的原因对所有人都很明显。

items.example: The verb is the common root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的共同词根。

items.example: It directs the appearing towards the viewer.
Parere supplies the visible half of the word.
items.exampleCN: parere 提供了这个词中「可见」的那一半。

items.example: A light appeared on the far shore.

items.meaning: the act of appearing; outward look
items.example: The building has a plain appearance.

items.meaning: seemingly; as far as one can tell
items.exampleCN: 看来那趟火车被取消了。

items.meaningCN: 突然显现的幽灵或幻影
items.example: An apparition stood at the end of the corridor.
items.exampleCN: 走廊尽头立着一个幻影。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词的后缀，表示「处于某种状态」
items.example: It turns the verb into a state of being visible.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成「处于可见状态」的形容词。

latinEntries.example: Apparere is the direct source of apparent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: apparere 是 apparent 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Parere sits inside the longer verb.
latinEntries.exampleCN: parere 嵌在那个更长的动词里。
